pt.root.security.meta.title: Security
pt.root.security.meta.description: How Auth secures authentication infrastructure: token architecture, key rotation, rate limiting, the hash-chained audit ledger, and how to report a vulnerability.
pt.root.security.hero.title: Security is the mechanism list.
pt.root.security.hero.lead: We do not ask you to trust marketing claims — every protection below names exactly how it works and where it runs. If we cannot describe the mechanism, we do not make the claim.
pt.root.security.layers[0].title: Token architecture
pt.root.security.layers[0].points[0]: Authorization codes require PKCE (S256) on every request and are single-use with short expiry.
pt.root.security.layers[0].points[1]: Refresh tokens rotate on every use; presenting a consumed token revokes the entire token family.
pt.root.security.layers[0].points[2]: Access and ID tokens are RS256 JWTs signed per environment; public keys are published at /.well-known/jwks.json.
pt.root.security.layers[0].points[3]: Revocation is available at /oauth/revoke for refresh tokens.
pt.root.security.layers[1].title: Sessions
pt.root.security.layers[1].points[0]: Session cookies are http-only, SameSite=Lax, secure in production, and carry signed RS256 session JWTs.
pt.root.security.layers[1].points[1]: Every session has both an idle timeout and an absolute expiry.
pt.root.security.layers[1].points[2]: Sessions are revocable server-side; logout revokes immediately.
pt.root.security.layers[2].title: Keys & secrets
pt.root.security.layers[2].points[0]: Per-environment RS256 signing keys; private keys are envelope-encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) and never logged.
pt.root.security.layers[2].points[1]: Rotation retires active keys while keeping them published so outstanding tokens verify until natural expiry.
pt.root.security.layers[2].points[2]: Client secrets are stored only as encrypted material; verification is constant-time compared after decryption.
pt.root.security.layers[3].title: Abuse controls
pt.root.security.layers[3].points[0]: Fixed-window rate limits: code delivery per email and per IP, verification failures per email, token issuance per client and IP.
pt.root.security.layers[3].points[1]: Excessive verification failures consume all outstanding one-time codes for that address.
pt.root.security.layers[3].points[2]: User-facing error copy stays neutral; specifics are written to server logs only.
pt.root.security.layers[4].title: Auditability
pt.root.security.layers[4].points[0]: Security events are written to a per-environment hash-chained ledger: each entry commits to its predecessor by SHA-256.
pt.root.security.layers[4].points[1]: The chain can be recomputed from genesis at any time; any retroactive edit breaks it.
pt.root.security.layers[4].points[2]: Standard auth events (logins, token issuance, reuse detection, revocation, key creation) are recorded alongside the ledger.
pt.root.security.layers[5].title: Data handling
pt.root.security.layers[5].points[0]: Tenant data lives in a Neon Postgres database in the region selected for the deployment; access requires encrypted transport.
pt.root.security.layers[5].points[1]: Secrets are envelope-encrypted before storage; the master key lives outside the database.
pt.root.security.layers[5].points[2]: No third-party trackers or ad pixels run on auth surfaces; analytics on this marketing site are cookieless and aggregated.
pt.root.security.complianceNote: Compliance status, honestly: Auth implements controls aligned with SOC 2 criteria from day one, but no certification audit has been completed yet. We will publish results here when that changes.
pt.root.security.disclosure.title: Found a hole? Tell us.
pt.root.security.disclosure.items[0]: Email hello@sdk.enterprises with [security] in the subject line.
pt.root.security.disclosure.items[1]: Include reproduction steps; we acknowledge reports within 2 business days.
pt.root.security.disclosure.items[2]: Please avoid automated scanning against production and do not access data beyond what proves the issue.
pt.root.security.disclosure.items[3]: Good-faith research under this policy is safe from legal action; we credit reporters unless they prefer anonymity.

it.root.home.hero.lead: Auth gives your product OIDC and OAuth 2.1 out of the box — hosted login pages, session management, and a management API — so your team ships features instead of identity plumbing.
it.root.home.hero.visual.footnote: PKCE mandatory · tokens verified against public JWKS
it.root.home.standards.sentence: We implement the specs exactly: PKCE on every authorization code, rotating refresh tokens, revocable signed sessions, published signing keys.
it.root.home.features.title: Identity plumbing, handled.
it.root.home.features.intro: Everything below is live today unless marked otherwise — each card names the mechanism, because that is what you are actually buying.
it.root.home.features.items[0].title: Universal login
it.root.home.features.items[0].body: A hosted sign-in flow your users get redirected to — email one-time codes, no passwords to store, no login UI to maintain.
it.root.home.features.items[1].title: Session management
it.root.home.features.items[1].body: Sessions are signed RS256 JWTs in http-only cookies, with idle and absolute expiry, server-side revocation, and per-environment keys.
it.root.home.features.items[2].title: Token security
it.root.home.features.items[2].body: Authorization codes always travel with PKCE. Refresh tokens rotate on every use, and a replayed token revokes its whole family.
it.root.home.features.items[3].title: Audit ledger
it.root.home.features.items[3].body: Every security event lands in a hash-chained audit log per environment — tampering breaks the chain, and the chain recomputes from genesis.
it.root.home.features.items[4].title: Abuse controls
it.root.home.features.items[4].body: Fixed-window rate limits on code delivery, verification attempts, and token issuance. Lockouts consume outstanding codes; copy stays neutral.
it.root.home.features.items[5].title: Management API
it.root.home.features.items[5].body: One API surface for applications, users, sessions, and logs at /api/v2, driven by scoped machine tokens.
it.root.home.privacy.title: Your tenants' data stays yours.
it.root.home.privacy.intro: Auth is identity infrastructure — we process exactly what authentication requires and publish every detail. No ad trackers, no data sale, no model training on tenant data.
it.root.home.privacy.processed[0]: Account email, to deliver one-time codes

it.root.home.quickstart.title: Three requests to a working login.
it.root.home.quickstart.intro: No proprietary protocol, no vendor lock-in — everything below is stock OAuth 2.1 and OIDC against our live endpoints.
it.root.home.quickstart.steps[0].title: Discover our endpoints
it.root.home.quickstart.steps[0].body: Your app reads standard OIDC discovery — no SDK required, any language works.
it.root.home.quickstart.steps[1].title: Send users to /authorize with PKCE
it.root.home.quickstart.steps[1].body: Create a code challenge, redirect the browser, we handle the hosted login and email code.
it.root.home.quickstart.steps[2].title: Exchange the code for tokens
it.root.home.quickstart.steps[2].body: Verify the id_token against our public JWKS, keep the refresh token, call userinfo when you need claims.
it.root.home.pricing.title: Priced by users, not by locks.
it.root.home.pricing.intro: Early-access pricing. A monthly active user is a user who authenticated at least once that month; you are never billed for stored-but-idle accounts.
it.root.home.pricing.plans[0].features[3]: Audit ledger and auth event logs
it.root.home.pricing.plans[1].features[2]: MFA, passkeys, and enterprise SSO as they ship
it.root.home.pricing.note: Billing is not yet automated — early-access tenants are invoiced manually and can leave anytime.
it.root.home.ctaBand.title: Your login page is one redirect away.
it.root.home.ctaBand.body: Point discovery at auth.sdk.enterprises and ship your first flow this afternoon.

it.root.legal.cookies.title: Cookies & tracking
it.root.legal.cookies.description: Auth surfaces are built to work without tracking you. This page lists every cookie and every analytics mechanism, which is a very short list.
it.root.legal.cookies.sections[0].heading: 1. Cookies we set
it.root.legal.cookies.sections[0].content[0: Essential. Keeps you signed in to your tenant dashboard; signed, http-only, expires with the session.
Essential. Issued only when you sign in to a product that uses Auth, scoped to that product's authentication.
it.root.legal.cookies.sections[0].content[1: There is no consent banner because there is nothing to consent to: no advertising cookies, no cross-site trackers, no social widgets, and no fingerprinting scripts run on auth.sdk.enterprises or on hosted login pages.
it.root.legal.cookies.sections[1].heading: 2. Analytics
it.root.legal.cookies.sections[1].content[0: The marketing pages use Vercel Analytics, which is cookieless: it counts page views in aggregate without storing identifiers or building profiles of individuals. No analytics runs on universal login pages, API endpoints, or inside tenants' applications.
it.root.legal.cookies.sections[2].heading: 3. Server-side records
it.root.legal.cookies.sections[2].content[0: Like any web server we log requests for security operations (abuse detection, rate limiting, audit evidence) under our retention rules in the privacy policy. These logs are not used to profile visitors of this marketing site.
it.root.legal.cookies.sections[3].heading: 4. Questions
it.root.legal.cookies.sections[3].content[0: Write to hello@sdk.enterprises if anything here is unclear.

it.root.legal.dpa.title: Data processing addendum
it.root.legal.dpa.description: This addendum sets out the terms on which SDK Enterprises processes personal data on behalf of tenants of the Auth service. It reflects the requirements applicable to processors under data protection law, including Article 28 of the General Data Protection Regulation.
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[0].heading: 1. Parties and roles
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[0].content[0]: This addendum is between you (the controller, "Customer") and SDK Enterprises (the processor). It applies to personal data that SDK Enterprises processes on your behalf when you use the Service to authenticate your end users. It forms part of the Agreement and prevails over it on matters of data protection.
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].heading: 2. Details of processing
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][0]: Subject matter: authentication and identity services for Customer applications.
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][1]: Duration: the term of the Agreement, plus retention duties described below.
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][2]: Nature and purpose: delivery of sign-in flows, verification of identity through one-time codes, issuance and management of sessions and tokens, abuse prevention, security logging, and associated support.
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][3]: Categories of data subjects: Customer's end users, and Customer personnel administering the tenant.
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][4]: Categories of personal data: identification data (notably email addresses), authentication and usage records, technical metadata such as IP address and user-agent, security and audit records, and transient abuse-prevention indicators.
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][5]: Special categories: none are requested or expected; Customer must not submit them.
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[2].heading: 3. Processor obligations
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[2].content[0]: SDK Enterprises processes personal data only on documented instructions from Customer — constituted by this addendum and Customer's configuration of the Service — unless required otherwise by Union or Member State law, in which case SDK Enterprises informs Customer of that legal requirement before processing unless legally prohibited. SDK Enterprises informs Customer without delay if it believes an instruction infringes applicable data protection law.
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[3].heading: 4. Confidentiality
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[3].content[0]: Persons authorised to process personal data do so only as necessary for the Service and are bound by confidentiality obligations that survive the end of their engagement.
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[4].heading: 5. Security measures
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[4].content[0]: Taking into account the state of the art and the costs of implementation, SDK Enterprises maintains appropriate technical and organisational measures, including: encryption of data in transit and appropriate encryption at rest; strict access control on a need-to-know basis; segregation of tenant environments; measures for availability and resilience, including backups and recovery procedures; abuse detection and rate limiting; tamper-evident logging of security-relevant events; and regular review of these measures as the Service evolves. A plain-language overview is published at /security.
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[5].heading: 6. Subprocessors
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[5].content[0]: Customer grants general written authorisation to engage subprocessors, whose identities, roles, and locations are published at /legal/subprocessors. SDK Enterprises imposes on each subprocessor, in writing, data protection obligations no less protective than those in this addendum and remains liable to Customer for subprocessor failures. At least fourteen (14) days before a new subprocessor processes personal data, SDK Enterprises updates the published list, giving Customer the opportunity to object on reasonable, data-protection-related grounds; if an objection cannot reasonably be resolved, Customer may terminate the affected part of the Service.
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].heading: 7. Assistance to Customer
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][0]: Requests from data subjects (access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection, portability): SDK Enterprises assists without undue delay, through available tenant tooling where possible.
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][1]: Data protection impact assessments and prior consultations: SDK Enterprises provides reasonably available information about the Service.
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][2]: Security incidents: SDK Enterprises notifies Customer without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting Customer's data, provides information reasonably required for Customer's own obligations, and cooperates in managing the incident.
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[7].heading: 8. International transfers
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[7].content[0]: Where personal data would be transferred outside the European Economic Area to a country not benefiting from an adequacy decision, SDK Enterprises ensures appropriate safeguards are in place — principally the standard contractual clauses adopted by the European Commission, entered into between the relevant exporter and importer — together with supplementary technical measures where needed. Current transfer locations are described on the subprocessors page.
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[8].heading: 9. Accountability and audits
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[8].content[0]: SDK Enterprises keeps records of processing activities within its scope and makes available documentation demonstrating compliance with this addendum. Customer may request such information once per year, and additionally following a personal data breach or a substantiated compliance concern. On-site audits, where granted, take place at Customer's cost, on reasonable notice, and subject to confidentiality and the protections owed to other customers.
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[9].heading: 10. Return and deletion
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[9].content[0]: On termination of the Agreement, SDK Enterprises makes Customer's personal data available for export and then deletes it, including within subprocessor systems, within a commercially reasonable period — save where retention is required by law, in which case the data remains protected under this addendum until deletion becomes possible.
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[10].heading: 11. Liability, law, and disputes
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[10].content[0]: Liability under this addendum is allocated and limited as set out in the terms of service. This addendum is governed by French law, and disputes follow the resolution mechanism agreed there.
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[11].heading: 12. California privacy rights
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[11].content[0]: For personal data subject to the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended, SDK Enterprises acts as a service provider: it does not sell or share personal data, does not retain, use, or disclose it outside the direct business relationship except as permitted by law, and does not combine it with personal data received from other sources.
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[12].heading: 13. Precedence and amendments
it.root.legal.dpa.sections[12].content[0]: If individual provisions of this addendum conflict with the standard contractual clauses incorporated under section 8, the clauses prevail for the transfers they govern. We may amend this addendum prospectively to reflect changes in the Service or law, announcing material changes on this page before they take effect.

it.root.legal.privacy.title: Privacy policy
it.root.legal.privacy.description: This policy explains what personal data the Auth service processes, why it is processed, how long it is kept, who it is shared with, and the rights available to the people concerned. We have written it to be read and understood, not merely displayed.
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[0].heading: 1. Who we are
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[0].content[0: The Auth service (the "Service") is operated by SDK Enterprises (SADDEK Entreprises, RCS Paris 850 513 912, whose registered office is at 44 Rue Pasquier, 75008 Paris, France — "SDK Enterprises", "we", "us"). Our customers use the Service to authenticate their own users; this document describes how personal data flows through that arrangement and what each party is responsible for.
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[1].heading: 2. Our role depends on the situation
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[1].content[0: For visitors to this website and for individuals who open or administer an account with us, SDK Enterprises determines why and how personal data is processed and acts as a data controller.

For end users who sign in to a product or service powered by Auth, our customer remains responsible for that processing as controller, and SDK Enterprises processes personal data on their documented instructions as a data processor, under our data processing addendum. If you are such an end user, your first point of contact is the product you were signing in to; we support them in answering your request without undue delay.
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[2].heading: 3. Categories of personal data we process
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[2].content[0: Account data. Email address and basic profile elements you or your provider choose to submit; authentication timestamps and usage counters relating to your account.

Authentication data. Records of sign-in attempts and outcomes, issuance and revocation of tokens and sessions, and related technical metadata (including IP address, browser user-agent, and precise timestamps) retained for security, abuse prevention, and evidence purposes.
Security records. Tamper-evident logs of security-relevant events associated with your account or environment.
Abuse-prevention data. Short-lived technical counters used to detect and throttle abusive traffic.
Communications data. The content of messages you send us (for example requests for support or the exercise of rights) and our replies.
Commercial data. Invoicing and payment references where a paid plan applies, handled through our invoicing process.
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[2].content[1: We do not require or store passwords for sign-in to the Service. Sensitive categories of personal data (health, biometrics, political opinions, and similar) are not requested and must not be submitted to us.
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[3].heading: 4. Purposes and legal bases
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[3].content[0: Operating and providing the Service — performance of a contract, or steps prior to entering into one.
Securing accounts, detecting fraud and abuse, and keeping security records — our legitimate interest in operating trustworthy infrastructure, balanced against your rights and expectations.
Meeting accounting, tax, and other statutory duties — compliance with a legal obligation.
Sending service communications relating to your account or incidents affecting it — performance of the contract; we do not send marketing email absent separate consent.
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[3].content[1: Where processing relies on consent, you may withdraw it at any time without affecting the lawfulness of processing carried out before withdrawal. We do not carry out automated decision-making producing legal effects within the meaning of applicable law.
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[4].heading: 5. Retention
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[4].content[0: Personal data is kept only as long as necessary for the purposes set out above. Account data is kept while an account or tenant remains active; security and audit records are kept while needed to evidence the integrity of the Service and meet legal requirements; abuse-prevention data is transient by design; commercial records are kept for the statutorily required bookkeeping periods. Data that is no longer needed is deleted or irreversibly anonymised.
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[5].heading: 6. Recipients and subprocessors
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[5].content[0: We share personal data only with: processors acting under contract on our behalf (hosting, database, cache, and email-delivery providers — identified individually on our subprocessors page); professional advisers under duties of confidentiality; and public authorities where a binding legal request requires it, in which case we notify those concerned unless legally prohibited. We never sell, rent, or broker personal data, and we do not use customer or end-user data for advertising or for training machine-learning models.
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[6].heading: 7. International transfers
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[6].content[0: Some of our providers operate outside the European Economic Area. Where personal data is transferred out of the EEA, we rely on an adequate adequacy decision or on appropriate safeguards — in particular the European Commission's standard contractual clauses — together with supplementary measures where required. The current list of providers and their locations is published on our subprocessors page.
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[7].heading: 8. Security of processing
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[7].content[0: We apply appropriate technical and organisational measures against unauthorised access, loss, alteration, or disclosure — including encryption in transit and at rest, strict access controls on a need-to-know basis, segregation of tenant data, rate limiting and abuse detection, and tamper-evident audit logging. Measures are reviewed as the Service evolves; a plain-language overview is available on our security page.
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].heading: 9. Your rights
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[0: Subject to applicable law, including the General Data Protection Regulation if you are in the EEA, you may ask us to:
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[1: give you access to the personal data we hold about you;
rectify inaccurate data or complete incomplete data;
erase data that is no longer lawfully processed;
restrict or object to particular processing;
provide your data in a structured, commonly used, portable format;
tell you about the recipients of your data and the safeguards applied.
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[2: Write to hello@sdk.enterprises. We respond within one month of a substantiated request and may ask for minimal proof of identity where necessary. You may also lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority — in France, the Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CNIL).
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[9].heading: 10. Children
it.root.legal.privacy.sections[9].content[0: The Service is directed at businesses and professionals. We do not knowingly process the personal data of children below the age of digital consent in the relevant jurisdiction; if you believe this has happened, contact us and we will delete the data promptly.

it.root.legal.privacy.sections[10].content[: We update this policy when our processing changes. Material changes are announced on this page, with a new effective date, before they take effect. Earlier versions are available on request.

it.root.security.hero.title: Security is the mechanism list.
it.root.security.hero.lead: We do not ask you to trust marketing claims — every protection below names exactly how it works and where it runs. If we cannot describe the mechanism, we do not make the claim.
it.root.security.layers[0].title: Token architecture
it.root.security.layers[0].points[0]: Authorization codes require PKCE (S256) on every request and are single-use with short expiry.
it.root.security.layers[0].points[1]: Refresh tokens rotate on every use; presenting a consumed token revokes the entire token family.
it.root.security.layers[0].points[2]: Access and ID tokens are RS256 JWTs signed per environment; public keys are published at /.well-known/jwks.json.
it.root.security.layers[0].points[3]: Revocation is available at /oauth/revoke for refresh tokens.
it.root.security.layers[1].title: Sessions
it.root.security.layers[1].points[0]: Session cookies are http-only, SameSite=Lax, secure in production, and carry signed RS256 session JWTs.
it.root.security.layers[1].points[1]: Every session has both an idle timeout and an absolute expiry.
it.root.security.layers[1].points[2]: Sessions are revocable server-side; logout revokes immediately.
it.root.security.layers[2].title: Keys & secrets
it.root.security.layers[2].points[0]: Per-environment RS256 signing keys; private keys are envelope-encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) and never logged.
it.root.security.layers[2].points[1]: Rotation retires active keys while keeping them published so outstanding tokens verify until natural expiry.
it.root.security.layers[2].points[2]: Client secrets are stored only as encrypted material; verification is constant-time compared after decryption.
it.root.security.layers[3].title: Abuse controls
it.root.security.layers[3].points[0]: Fixed-window rate limits: code delivery per email and per IP, verification failures per email, token issuance per client and IP.
it.root.security.layers[3].points[1]: Excessive verification failures consume all outstanding one-time codes for that address.
it.root.security.layers[3].points[2]: User-facing error copy stays neutral; specifics are written to server logs only.
it.root.security.layers[4].title: Auditability
it.root.security.layers[4].points[0]: Security events are written to a per-environment hash-chained ledger: each entry commits to its predecessor by SHA-256.
it.root.security.layers[4].points[1]: The chain can be recomputed from genesis at any time; any retroactive edit breaks it.
it.root.security.layers[4].points[2]: Standard auth events (logins, token issuance, reuse detection, revocation, key creation) are recorded alongside the ledger.
it.root.security.layers[5].title: Data handling
it.root.security.layers[5].points[0]: Tenant data lives in a Neon Postgres database in the region selected for the deployment; access requires encrypted transport.
it.root.security.layers[5].points[1]: Secrets are envelope-encrypted before storage; the master key lives outside the database.
it.root.security.layers[5].points[2]: No third-party trackers or ad pixels run on auth surfaces; analytics on this marketing site are cookieless and aggregated.
it.root.security.complianceNote: Compliance status, honestly: Auth implements controls aligned with SOC 2 criteria from day one, but no certification audit has been completed yet. We will publish results here when that changes.
it.root.security.disclosure.title: Found a hole? Tell us.
it.root.security.disclosure.items[0]: Email hello@sdk.enterprises with [security] in the subject line.
it.root.security.disclosure.items[1]: Include reproduction steps; we acknowledge reports within 2 business days.
it.root.security.disclosure.items[2]: Please avoid automated scanning against production and do not access data beyond what proves the issue.
it.root.security.disclosure.items[3]: Good-faith research under this policy is safe from legal action; we credit reporters unless they prefer anonymity.

nl.root.home.meta.description: Auth gives your product OIDC and OAuth 2.1 out of the box — hosted login pages, session management, and a management API — so your team ships features instead of identity plumbing.
nl.root.home.hero.title: One login flow for every tenant you host.
nl.root.home.hero.lead: Auth gives your product OIDC and OAuth 2.1 out of the box — hosted login pages, session management, and a management API — so your team ships features instead of identity plumbing.
nl.root.home.hero.visual.footnote: PKCE mandatory · tokens verified against public JWKS
nl.root.home.standards.sentence: We implement the specs exactly: PKCE on every authorization code, rotating refresh tokens, revocable signed sessions, published signing keys.
nl.root.home.features.title: Identity plumbing, handled.
nl.root.home.features.intro: Everything below is live today unless marked otherwise — each card names the mechanism, because that is what you are actually buying.
nl.root.home.features.items[0].title: Universal login
nl.root.home.features.items[0].body: A hosted sign-in flow your users get redirected to — email one-time codes, no passwords to store, no login UI to maintain.
nl.root.home.features.items[1].title: Session management
nl.root.home.features.items[1].body: Sessions are signed RS256 JWTs in http-only cookies, with idle and absolute expiry, server-side revocation, and per-environment keys.
nl.root.home.features.items[2].title: Token security
nl.root.home.features.items[2].body: Authorization codes always travel with PKCE. Refresh tokens rotate on every use, and a replayed token revokes its whole family.
nl.root.home.features.items[3].title: Audit ledger
nl.root.home.features.items[3].body: Every security event lands in a hash-chained audit log per environment — tampering breaks the chain, and the chain recomputes from genesis.
nl.root.home.features.items[4].title: Abuse controls
nl.root.home.features.items[4].body: Fixed-window rate limits on code delivery, verification attempts, and token issuance. Lockouts consume outstanding codes; copy stays neutral.
nl.root.home.features.items[5].title: Management API
nl.root.home.features.items[5].body: One API surface for applications, users, sessions, and logs at /api/v2, driven by scoped machine tokens.
nl.root.home.privacy.title: Your tenants' data stays yours.
nl.root.home.privacy.intro: Auth is identity infrastructure — we process exactly what authentication requires and publish every detail. No ad trackers, no data sale, no model training on tenant data.
nl.root.home.privacy.processed[0]: Account email, to deliver one-time codes
nl.root.home.privacy.processed[1]: Authentication events with technical metadata, kept for security and audit
nl.root.home.privacy.processed[2]: Transient abuse-prevention counters that expire on their own
nl.root.home.privacy.processed[3]: Credentials and cryptographic keys stored only in protected form
nl.root.home.privacy.never[0]: Sell, rent, or share personal data — ever, for any purpose
nl.root.home.privacy.never[1]: Load third-party trackers or ad pixels on auth surfaces
nl.root.home.privacy.never[2]: Train models on tenant or end-user data
nl.root.home.privacy.never[3]: Keep data after you close your account, beyond legal minimums
nl.root.home.quickstart.title: Three requests to a working login.
nl.root.home.quickstart.intro: No proprietary protocol, no vendor lock-in — everything below is stock OAuth 2.1 and OIDC against our live endpoints.
nl.root.home.quickstart.steps[0].title: Discover our endpoints
nl.root.home.quickstart.steps[0].body: Your app reads standard OIDC discovery — no SDK required, any language works.
nl.root.home.quickstart.steps[1].title: Send users to /authorize with PKCE
nl.root.home.quickstart.steps[1].body: Create a code challenge, redirect the browser, we handle the hosted login and email code.
nl.root.home.quickstart.steps[2].title: Exchange the code for tokens
nl.root.home.quickstart.steps[2].body: Verify the id_token against our public JWKS, keep the refresh token, call userinfo when you need claims.
nl.root.home.pricing.title: Priced by users, not by locks.
nl.root.home.pricing.intro: Early-access pricing. A monthly active user is a user who authenticated at least once that month; you are never billed for stored-but-idle accounts.
nl.root.home.pricing.plans[0].features[3]: Audit ledger and auth event logs
nl.root.home.pricing.plans[1].features[2]: MFA, passkeys, and enterprise SSO as they ship
nl.root.home.pricing.note: Billing is not yet automated — early-access tenants are invoiced manually and can leave anytime.
nl.root.home.ctaBand.title: Your login page is one redirect away.
nl.root.home.ctaBand.body: Point discovery at auth.sdk.enterprises and ship your first flow this afternoon.

nl.root.legal.dpa.title: Data processing addendum
nl.root.legal.dpa.description: This addendum sets out the terms on which SDK Enterprises processes personal data on behalf of tenants of the Auth service. It reflects the requirements applicable to processors under data protection law, including Article 28 of the General Data Protection Regulation.
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[0].heading: 1. Parties and roles
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[0].content[0]: This addendum is between you (the controller, "Customer") and SDK Enterprises (the processor). It applies to personal data that SDK Enterprises processes on your behalf when you use the Service to authenticate your end users. It forms part of the Agreement and prevails over it on matters of data protection.
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].heading: 2. Details of processing
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][0]: Subject matter: authentication and identity services for Customer applications.
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][1]: Duration: the term of the Agreement, plus retention duties described below.
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][2]: Nature and purpose: delivery of sign-in flows, verification of identity through one-time codes, issuance and management of sessions and tokens, abuse prevention, security logging, and associated support.
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][3]: Categories of data subjects: Customer's end users, and Customer personnel administering the tenant.
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][4]: Categories of personal data: identification data (notably email addresses), authentication and usage records, technical metadata such as IP address and user-agent, security and audit records, and transient abuse-prevention indicators.
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][5]: Special categories: none are requested or expected; Customer must not submit them.
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[2].heading: 3. Processor obligations
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[2].content[0]: SDK Enterprises processes personal data only on documented instructions from Customer — constituted by this addendum and Customer's configuration of the Service — unless required otherwise by Union or Member State law, in which case SDK Enterprises informs Customer of that legal requirement before processing unless legally prohibited. SDK Enterprises informs Customer without delay if it believes an instruction infringes applicable data protection law.
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[3].heading: 4. Confidentiality
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[3].content[0]: Persons authorised to process personal data do so only as necessary for the Service and are bound by confidentiality obligations that survive the end of their engagement.
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[4].heading: 5. Security measures
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[4].content[0]: Taking into account the state of the art and the costs of implementation, SDK Enterprises maintains appropriate technical and organisational measures, including: encryption of data in transit and appropriate encryption at rest; strict access control on a need-to-know basis; segregation of tenant environments; measures for availability and resilience, including backups and recovery procedures; abuse detection and rate limiting; tamper-evident logging of security-relevant events; and regular review of these measures as the Service evolves. A plain-language overview is published at /security.
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[5].heading: 6. Subprocessors
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[5].content[0]: Customer grants general written authorisation to engage subprocessors, whose identities, roles, and locations are published at /legal/subprocessors. SDK Enterprises imposes on each subprocessor, in writing, data protection obligations no less protective than those in this addendum and remains liable to Customer for subprocessor failures. At least fourteen (14) days before a new subprocessor processes personal data, SDK Enterprises updates the published list, giving Customer the opportunity to object on reasonable, data-protection-related grounds; if an objection cannot reasonably be resolved, Customer may terminate the affected part of the Service.
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].heading: 7. Assistance to Customer
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][0]: Requests from data subjects (access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection, portability): SDK Enterprises assists without undue delay, through available tenant tooling where possible.
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][1]: Data protection impact assessments and prior consultations: SDK Enterprises provides reasonably available information about the Service.
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][2]: Security incidents: SDK Enterprises notifies Customer without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting Customer's data, provides information reasonably required for Customer's own obligations, and cooperates in managing the incident.
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[7].heading: 8. International transfers
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[7].content[0]: Where personal data would be transferred outside the European Economic Area to a country not benefiting from an adequacy decision, SDK Enterprises ensures appropriate safeguards are in place — principally the standard contractual clauses adopted by the European Commission, entered into between the relevant exporter and importer — together with supplementary technical measures where needed. Current transfer locations are described on the subprocessors page.
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[8].heading: 9. Accountability and audits
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[8].content[0]: SDK Enterprises keeps records of processing activities within its scope and makes available documentation demonstrating compliance with this addendum. Customer may request such information once per year, and additionally following a personal data breach or a substantiated compliance concern. On-site audits, where granted, take place at Customer's cost, on reasonable notice, and subject to confidentiality and the protections owed to other customers.
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[9].heading: 10. Return and deletion
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[9].content[0]: On termination of the Agreement, SDK Enterprises makes Customer's personal data available for export and then deletes it, including within subprocessor systems, within a commercially reasonable period — save where retention is required by law, in which case the data remains protected under this addendum until deletion becomes possible.
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[10].heading: 11. Liability, law, and disputes
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[10].content[0]: Liability under this addendum is allocated and limited as set out in the terms of service. This addendum is governed by French law, and disputes follow the resolution mechanism agreed there.
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[11].heading: 12. California privacy rights
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[11].content[0]: For personal data subject to the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended, SDK Enterprises acts as a service provider: it does not sell or share personal data, does not retain, use, or disclose it outside the direct business relationship except as permitted by law, and does not combine it with personal data received from other sources.
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[12].heading: 13. Precedence and amendments
nl.root.legal.dpa.sections[12].content[0]: If individual provisions of this addendum conflict with the standard contractual clauses incorporated under section 8, the clauses prevail for the transfers they govern. We may amend this addendum prospectively to reflect changes in the Service or law, announcing material changes on this page before they take effect.

nl.root.legal.privacy.title: Privacy policy
nl.root.legal.privacy.description: This policy explains what personal data the Auth service processes, why it is processed, how long it is kept, who it is shared with, and the rights available to the people concerned. We have written it to be read and understood, not merely displayed.
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[0].heading: 1. Who we are
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[0].content[0: The Auth service (the "Service") is operated by SDK Enterprises (SADDEK Entreprises, RCS Paris 850 513 912, whose registered office is at 44 Rue Pasquier, 75008 Paris, France — "SDK Enterprises", "we", "us"). Our customers use the Service to authenticate their own users; this document describes how personal data flows through that arrangement and what each party is responsible for.
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[1].heading: 2. Our role depends on the situation
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[1].content[0: For visitors to this website and for individuals who open or administer an account with us, SDK Enterprises determines why and how personal data is processed and acts as a data controller.

For end users who sign in to a product or service powered by Auth, our customer remains responsible for that processing as controller, and SDK Enterprises processes personal data on their documented instructions as a data processor, under our data processing addendum. If you are such an end user, your first point of contact is the product you were signing in to; we support them in answering your request without undue delay.
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[2].heading: 3. Categories of personal data we process
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[2].content[0: Account data. Email address and basic profile elements you or your provider choose to submit; authentication timestamps and usage counters relating to your account.

Authentication data. Records of sign-in attempts and outcomes, issuance and revocation of tokens and sessions, and related technical metadata (including IP address, browser user-agent, and precise timestamps) retained for security, abuse prevention, and evidence purposes.
Security records. Tamper-evident logs of security-relevant events associated with your account or environment.
Abuse-prevention data. Short-lived technical counters used to detect and throttle abusive traffic.
Communications data. The content of messages you send us (for example requests for support or the exercise of rights) and our replies.
Commercial data. Invoicing and payment references where a paid plan applies, handled through our invoicing process.
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[2].content[1: We do not require or store passwords for sign-in to the Service. Sensitive categories of personal data (health, biometrics, political opinions, and similar) are not requested and must not be submitted to us.
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[3].heading: 4. Purposes and legal bases
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[3].content[0: Operating and providing the Service — performance of a contract, or steps prior to entering into one.
Securing accounts, detecting fraud and abuse, and keeping security records — our legitimate interest in operating trustworthy infrastructure, balanced against your rights and expectations.
Meeting accounting, tax, and other statutory duties — compliance with a legal obligation.
Sending service communications relating to your account or incidents affecting it — performance of the contract; we do not send marketing email absent separate consent.
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[3].content[1: Where processing relies on consent, you may withdraw it at any time without affecting the lawfulness of processing carried out before withdrawal. We do not carry out automated decision-making producing legal effects within the meaning of applicable law.
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[4].heading: 5. Retention
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[4].content[0: Personal data is kept only as long as necessary for the purposes set out above. Account data is kept while an account or tenant remains active; security and audit records are kept while needed to evidence the integrity of the Service and meet legal requirements; abuse-prevention data is transient by design; commercial records are kept for the statutorily required bookkeeping periods. Data that is no longer needed is deleted or irreversibly anonymised.
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[5].heading: 6. Recipients and subprocessors
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[5].content[0: We share personal data only with: processors acting under contract on our behalf (hosting, database, cache, and email-delivery providers — identified individually on our subprocessors page); professional advisers under duties of confidentiality; and public authorities where a binding legal request requires it, in which case we notify those concerned unless legally prohibited. We never sell, rent, or broker personal data, and we do not use customer or end-user data for advertising or for training machine-learning models.
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[6].heading: 7. International transfers
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[6].content[0: Some of our providers operate outside the European Economic Area. Where personal data is transferred out of the EEA, we rely on an adequate adequacy decision or on appropriate safeguards — in particular the European Commission's standard contractual clauses — together with supplementary measures where required. The current list of providers and their locations is published on our subprocessors page.
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[7].heading: 8. Security of processing
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[7].content[0: We apply appropriate technical and organisational measures against unauthorised access, loss, alteration, or disclosure — including encryption in transit and at rest, strict access controls on a need-to-know basis, segregation of tenant data, rate limiting and abuse detection, and tamper-evident audit logging. Measures are reviewed as the Service evolves; a plain-language overview is available on our security page.
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].heading: 9. Your rights
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[0: Subject to applicable law, including the General Data Protection Regulation if you are in the EEA, you may ask us to:
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[1: give you access to the personal data we hold about you;
rectify inaccurate data or complete incomplete data;
erase data that is no longer lawfully processed;
restrict or object to particular processing;
provide your data in a structured, commonly used, portable format;
tell you about the recipients of your data and the safeguards applied.
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[2: Write to hello@sdk.enterprises. We respond within one month of a substantiated request and may ask for minimal proof of identity where necessary. You may also lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority — in France, the Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CNIL).
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[9].heading: 10. Children
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[9].content[0: The Service is directed at businesses and professionals. We do not knowingly process the personal data of children below the age of digital consent in the relevant jurisdiction; if you believe this has happened, contact us and we will delete the data promptly.
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[10].heading: 11. Changes to this policy
nl.root.legal.privacy.sections[10].content[: We update this policy when our processing changes. Material changes are announced on this page, with a new effective date, before they take effect. Earlier versions are available on request.

nl.root.security.meta.title: Security
nl.root.security.meta.description: How Auth secures authentication infrastructure: token architecture, key rotation, rate limiting, the hash-chained audit ledger, and how to report a vulnerability.
nl.root.security.hero.title: Security is the mechanism list.
nl.root.security.hero.lead: We do not ask you to trust marketing claims — every protection below names exactly how it works and where it runs. If we cannot describe the mechanism, we do not make the claim.
nl.root.security.layers[0].title: Token architecture
nl.root.security.layers[0].points[0]: Authorization codes require PKCE (S256) on every request and are single-use with short expiry.
nl.root.security.layers[0].points[1]: Refresh tokens rotate on every use; presenting a consumed token revokes the entire token family.
nl.root.security.layers[0].points[2]: Access and ID tokens are RS256 JWTs signed per environment; public keys are published at /.well-known/jwks.json.
nl.root.security.layers[0].points[3]: Revocation is available at /oauth/revoke for refresh tokens.
nl.root.security.layers[1].title: Sessions
nl.root.security.layers[1].points[0]: Session cookies are http-only, SameSite=Lax, secure in production, and carry signed RS256 session JWTs.
nl.root.security.layers[1].points[1]: Every session has both an idle timeout and an absolute expiry.
nl.root.security.layers[1].points[2]: Sessions are revocable server-side; logout revokes immediately.
nl.root.security.layers[2].title: Keys & secrets
nl.root.security.layers[2].points[0]: Per-environment RS256 signing keys; private keys are envelope-encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) and never logged.
nl.root.security.layers[2].points[1]: Rotation retires active keys while keeping them published so outstanding tokens verify until natural expiry.
nl.root.security.layers[2].points[2]: Client secrets are stored only as encrypted material; verification is constant-time compared after decryption.
nl.root.security.layers[3].title: Abuse controls
nl.root.security.layers[3].points[0]: Fixed-window rate limits: code delivery per email and per IP, verification failures per email, token issuance per client and IP.
nl.root.security.layers[3].points[1]: Excessive verification failures consume all outstanding one-time codes for that address.
nl.root.security.layers[3].points[2]: User-facing error copy stays neutral; specifics are written to server logs only.
nl.root.security.layers[4].title: Auditability
nl.root.security.layers[4].points[0]: Security events are written to a per-environment hash-chained ledger: each entry commits to its predecessor by SHA-256.
nl.root.security.layers[4].points[1]: The chain can be recomputed from genesis at any time; any retroactive edit breaks it.
nl.root.security.layers[4].points[2]: Standard auth events (logins, token issuance, reuse detection, revocation, key creation) are recorded alongside the ledger.
nl.root.security.layers[5].title: Data handling
nl.root.security.layers[5].points[0]: Tenant data lives in a Neon Postgres database in the region selected for the deployment; access requires encrypted transport.
nl.root.security.layers[5].points[1]: Secrets are envelope-encrypted before storage; the master key lives outside the database.
nl.root.security.layers[5].points[2]: No third-party trackers or ad pixels run on auth surfaces; analytics on this marketing site are cookieless and aggregated.
nl.root.security.complianceNote: Compliance status, honestly: Auth implements controls aligned with SOC 2 criteria from day one, but no certification audit has been completed yet. We will publish results here when that changes.
nl.root.security.disclosure.title: Found a hole? Tell us.
nl.root.security.disclosure.items[0]: Email hello@sdk.enterprises with [security] in the subject line.
nl.root.security.disclosure.items[1]: Include reproduction steps; we acknowledge reports within 2 business days.
nl.root.security.disclosure.items[2]: Please avoid automated scanning against production and do not access data beyond what proves the issue.
nl.root.security.disclosure.items[3]: Good-faith research under this policy is safe from legal action; we credit reporters unless they prefer anonymity.

sv.root.home.features.items[2].title: Token security
sv.root.home.features.items[2].body: Authorization codes always travel with PKCE. Refresh tokens rotate on every use, and a replayed token revokes its whole family.
sv.root.home.features.items[3].title: Audit ledger
sv.root.home.features.items[3].body: Every security event lands in a hash-chained audit log per environment — tampering breaks the chain, and the chain recomputes from genesis.
sv.root.home.features.items[4].title: Abuse controls
sv.root.home.features.items[4].body: Fixed-window rate limits on code delivery, verification attempts, and token issuance. Lockouts consume outstanding codes; copy stays neutral.
sv.root.home.features.items[5].title: Management API

sv.root.legal.dpa.title: Data processing addendum
sv.root.legal.dpa.description: This addendum sets out the terms on which SDK Enterprises processes personal data on behalf of tenants of the Auth service. It reflects the requirements applicable to processors under data protection law, including Article 28 of the General Data Protection Regulation.
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[0].heading: 1. Parties and roles
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[0].content[0]: This addendum is between you (the controller, "Customer") and SDK Enterprises (the processor). It applies to personal data that SDK Enterprises processes on your behalf when you use the Service to authenticate your end users. It forms part of the Agreement and prevails over it on matters of data protection.
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].heading: 2. Details of processing
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][0]: Subject matter: authentication and identity services for Customer applications.
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][1]: Duration: the term of the Agreement, plus retention duties described below.
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][2]: Nature and purpose: delivery of sign-in flows, verification of identity through one-time codes, issuance and management of sessions and tokens, abuse prevention, security logging, and associated support.
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][3]: Categories of data subjects: Customer's end users, and Customer personnel administering the tenant.
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][4]: Categories of personal data: identification data (notably email addresses), authentication and usage records, technical metadata such as IP address and user-agent, security and audit records, and transient abuse-prevention indicators.
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][5]: Special categories: none are requested or expected; Customer must not submit them.
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[2].heading: 3. Processor obligations
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[2].content[0]: SDK Enterprises processes personal data only on documented instructions from Customer — constituted by this addendum and Customer's configuration of the Service — unless required otherwise by Union or Member State law, in which case SDK Enterprises informs Customer of that legal requirement before processing unless legally prohibited. SDK Enterprises informs Customer without delay if it believes an instruction infringes applicable data protection law.
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[3].heading: 4. Confidentiality
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[3].content[0]: Persons authorised to process personal data do so only as necessary for the Service and are bound by confidentiality obligations that survive the end of their engagement.
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[4].heading: 5. Security measures
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[4].content[0]: Taking into account the state of the art and the costs of implementation, SDK Enterprises maintains appropriate technical and organisational measures, including: encryption of data in transit and appropriate encryption at rest; strict access control on a need-to-know basis; segregation of tenant environments; measures for availability and resilience, including backups and recovery procedures; abuse detection and rate limiting; tamper-evident logging of security-relevant events; and regular review of these measures as the Service evolves. A plain-language overview is published at /security.
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[5].heading: 6. Subprocessors
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[5].content[0]: Customer grants general written authorisation to engage subprocessors, whose identities, roles, and locations are published at /legal/subprocessors. SDK Enterprises imposes on each subprocessor, in writing, data protection obligations no less protective than those in this addendum and remains liable to Customer for subprocessor failures. At least fourteen (14) days before a new subprocessor processes personal data, SDK Enterprises updates the published list, giving Customer the opportunity to object on reasonable, data-protection-related grounds; if an objection cannot reasonably be resolved, Customer may terminate the affected part of the Service.
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].heading: 7. Assistance to Customer
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][0]: Requests from data subjects (access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection, portability): SDK Enterprises assists without undue delay, through available tenant tooling where possible.
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][1]: Data protection impact assessments and prior consultations: SDK Enterprises provides reasonably available information about the Service.
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][2]: Security incidents: SDK Enterprises notifies Customer without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting Customer's data, provides information reasonably required for Customer's own obligations, and cooperates in managing the incident.
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[7].heading: 8. International transfers
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[7].content[0]: Where personal data would be transferred outside the European Economic Area to a country not benefiting from an adequacy decision, SDK Enterprises ensures appropriate safeguards are in place — principally the standard contractual clauses adopted by the European Commission, entered into between the relevant exporter and importer — together with supplementary technical measures where needed. Current transfer locations are described on the subprocessors page.
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[8].heading: 9. Accountability and audits
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[8].content[0]: SDK Enterprises keeps records of processing activities within its scope and makes available documentation demonstrating compliance with this addendum. Customer may request such information once per year, and additionally following a personal data breach or a substantiated compliance concern. On-site audits, where granted, take place at Customer's cost, on reasonable notice, and subject to confidentiality and the protections owed to other customers.
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[9].heading: 10. Return and deletion
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[9].content[0]: On termination of the Agreement, SDK Enterprises makes Customer's personal data available for export and then deletes it, including within subprocessor systems, within a commercially reasonable period — save where retention is required by law, in which case the data remains protected under this addendum until deletion becomes possible.
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[10].heading: 11. Liability, law, and disputes
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[10].content[0]: Liability under this addendum is allocated and limited as set out in the terms of service. This addendum is governed by French law, and disputes follow the resolution mechanism agreed there.
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[11].heading: 12. California privacy rights
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[11].content[0]: For personal data subject to the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended, SDK Enterprises acts as a service provider: it does not sell or share personal data, does not retain, use, or disclose it outside the direct business relationship except as permitted by law, and does not combine it with personal data received from other sources.
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[12].heading: 13. Precedence and amendments
sv.root.legal.dpa.sections[12].content[0]: If individual provisions of this addendum conflict with the standard contractual clauses incorporated under section 8, the clauses prevail for the transfers they govern. We may amend this addendum prospectively to reflect changes in the Service or law, announcing material changes on this page before they take effect.

Authentication data. Records of sign-in attempts and outcomes, issuance and revocation of tokens and sessions, and related technical metadata (including IP address, browser user-agent, and precise timestamps) retained for security, abuse prevention, and evidence purposes.
Security records. Tamper-evident logs of security-relevant events associated with your account or environment.
Abuse-prevention data. Short-lived technical counters used to detect and throttle abusive traffic.
Communications data. The content of messages you send us (for example requests for support or the exercise of rights) and our replies.
Commercial data. Invoicing and payment references where a paid plan applies, handled through our invoicing process.

Sending service communications relating to your account or incidents affecting it — performance of the contract; we do not send marketing email absent separate consent.
sv.root.legal.privacy.sections[3].content[1: Where processing relies on consent, you may withdraw it at any time without affecting the lawfulness of processing carried out before withdrawal. We do not carry out automated decision-making producing legal effects within the meaning of applicable law.
sv.root.legal.privacy.sections[4].heading: 5. Retention

Account data is kept while an account or tenant remains active; security and audit records are kept while needed to evidence the integrity of the Service and meet legal requirements; abuse-prevention data is transient by design; commercial records are kept for the statutorily required bookkeeping periods. Data that is no longer needed is deleted or irreversibly anonymised.

sv.root.legal.privacy.sections[5].content[0: We share personal data only with: processors acting under contract on our behalf (hosting, database, cache, and email-delivery providers — identified individually on our subprocessors page); professional advisers under duties of confidentiality; and public authorities where a binding legal request requires it, in which case we notify those concerned unless legally prohibited. We never sell, rent, or broker personal data, and we do not use customer or end-user data for advertising or for training machine-learning models.
sv.root.legal.privacy.sections[6].heading: 7. International transfers
sv.root.legal.privacy.sections[6].content[0: Some of our providers operate outside the European Economic Area. Where personal data is transferred out of the EEA, we rely on an adequate adequacy decision or on appropriate safeguards — in particular the European Commission's standard contractual clauses — together with supplementary measures where required. The current list of providers and their locations is published on our subprocessors page.
sv.root.legal.privacy.sections[7].heading: 8. Security of processing
sv.root.legal.privacy.sections[7].content[0: We apply appropriate technical and organisational measures against unauthorised access, loss, alteration, or disclosure — including encryption in transit and at rest, strict access controls on a need-to-know basis, segregation of tenant data, rate limiting and abuse detection, and tamper-evident audit logging. Measures are reviewed as the Service evolves; a plain-language overview is available on our security page.
sv.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].heading: 9. Your rights
sv.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[0: Subject to applicable law, including the General Data Protection Regulation if you are in the EEA, you may ask us to:
sv.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[1: give you access to the personal data we hold about you;
rectify inaccurate data or complete incomplete data;
erase data that is no longer lawfully processed;
restrict or object to particular processing;
provide your data in a structured, commonly used, portable format;
tell you about the recipients of your data and the safeguards applied.
sv.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[2: Write to hello@sdk.enterprises. We respond within one month of a substantiated request and may ask for minimal proof of identity where necessary. You may also lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority — in France, the Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CNIL).
sv.root.legal.privacy.sections[9].heading: 10. Children
sv.root.legal.privacy.sections[9].content[0: The Service is directed at businesses and professionals. We do not knowingly process the personal data of children below the age of digital consent in the relevant jurisdiction; if you believe this has happened, contact us and we will delete the data promptly.

sv.root.legal.privacy.sections[10].content[: We update this policy when our processing changes. Material changes are announced on this page, with a new effective date, before they take effect. Earlier versions are available on request.

sv.root.security.meta.title: Security
sv.root.security.meta.description: How Auth secures authentication infrastructure: token architecture, key rotation, rate limiting, the hash-chained audit ledger, and how to report a vulnerability.
sv.root.security.hero.title: Security is the mechanism list.
sv.root.security.hero.lead: We do not ask you to trust marketing claims — every protection below names exactly how it works and where it runs. If we cannot describe the mechanism, we do not make the claim.
sv.root.security.layers[0].title: Token architecture
sv.root.security.layers[0].points[0]: Authorization codes require PKCE (S256) on every request and are single-use with short expiry.
sv.root.security.layers[0].points[1]: Refresh tokens rotate on every use; presenting a consumed token revokes the entire token family.
sv.root.security.layers[0].points[2]: Access and ID tokens are RS256 JWTs signed per environment; public keys are published at /.well-known/jwks.json.
sv.root.security.layers[0].points[3]: Revocation is available at /oauth/revoke for refresh tokens.
sv.root.security.layers[1].title: Sessions
sv.root.security.layers[1].points[0]: Session cookies are http-only, SameSite=Lax, secure in production, and carry signed RS256 session JWTs.
sv.root.security.layers[1].points[1]: Every session has both an idle timeout and an absolute expiry.
sv.root.security.layers[1].points[2]: Sessions are revocable server-side; logout revokes immediately.
sv.root.security.layers[2].title: Keys & secrets
sv.root.security.layers[2].points[0]: Per-environment RS256 signing keys; private keys are envelope-encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) and never logged.
sv.root.security.layers[2].points[1]: Rotation retires active keys while keeping them published so outstanding tokens verify until natural expiry.
sv.root.security.layers[2].points[2]: Client secrets are stored only as encrypted material; verification is constant-time compared after decryption.
sv.root.security.layers[3].title: Abuse controls
sv.root.security.layers[3].points[0]: Fixed-window rate limits: code delivery per email and per IP, verification failures per email, token issuance per client and IP.
sv.root.security.layers[3].points[1]: Excessive verification failures consume all outstanding one-time codes for that address.
sv.root.security.layers[3].points[2]: User-facing error copy stays neutral; specifics are written to server logs only.
sv.root.security.layers[4].title: Auditability
sv.root.security.layers[4].points[0]: Security events are written to a per-environment hash-chained ledger: each entry commits to its predecessor by SHA-256.
sv.root.security.layers[4].points[1]: The chain can be recomputed from genesis at any time; any retroactive edit breaks it.
sv.root.security.layers[4].points[2]: Standard auth events (logins, token issuance, reuse detection, revocation, key creation) are recorded alongside the ledger.
sv.root.security.layers[5].title: Data handling
sv.root.security.layers[5].points[0]: Tenant data lives in a Neon Postgres database in the region selected for the deployment; access requires encrypted transport.
sv.root.security.layers[5].points[1]: Secrets are envelope-encrypted before storage; the master key lives outside the database.
sv.root.security.layers[5].points[2]: No third-party trackers or ad pixels run on auth surfaces; analytics on this marketing site are cookieless and aggregated.
sv.root.security.complianceNote: Compliance status, honestly: Auth implements controls aligned with SOC 2 criteria from day one, but no certification audit has been completed yet. We will publish results here when that changes.
sv.root.security.disclosure.title: Found a hole? Tell us.
sv.root.security.disclosure.items[0]: Email hello@sdk.enterprises with [security] in the subject line.
sv.root.security.disclosure.items[1]: Include reproduction steps; we acknowledge reports within 2 business days.
sv.root.security.disclosure.items[2]: Please avoid automated scanning against production and do not access data beyond what proves the issue.
sv.root.security.disclosure.items[3]: Good-faith research under this policy is safe from legal action; we credit reporters unless they prefer anonymity.

no.root.home.standards.sentence: We implement the specs exactly: PKCE on every authorization code, rotating refresh tokens, revocable signed sessions, published signing keys.
no.root.home.features.title: Identity plumbing, handled.
no.root.home.features.intro: Everything below is live today unless marked otherwise — each card names the mechanism, because that is what you are actually buying.
no.root.home.features.items[0].title: Universal login
no.root.home.features.items[0].body: A hosted sign-in flow your users get redirected to — email one-time codes, no passwords to store, no login UI to maintain.
no.root.home.features.items[1].title: Session management
no.root.home.features.items[1].body: Sessions are signed RS256 JWTs in http-only cookies, with idle and absolute expiry, server-side revocation, and per-environment keys.
no.root.home.features.items[2].title: Token security
no.root.home.features.items[2].body: Authorization codes always travel with PKCE. Refresh tokens rotate on every use, and a replayed token revokes its whole family.
no.root.home.features.items[3].title: Audit ledger
no.root.home.features.items[3].body: Every security event lands in a hash-chained audit log per environment — tampering breaks the chain, and the chain recomputes from genesis.
no.root.home.features.items[4].title: Abuse controls
no.root.home.features.items[4].body: Fixed-window rate limits on code delivery, verification attempts, and token issuance. Lockouts consume outstanding codes; copy stays neutral.
no.root.home.features.items[5].title: Management API
no.root.home.features.items[5].body: One API surface for applications, users, sessions, and logs at /api/v2, driven by scoped machine tokens.
no.root.home.privacy.title: Your tenants' data stays yours.
no.root.home.privacy.intro: Auth is identity infrastructure — we process exactly what authentication requires and publish every detail. No ad trackers, no data sale, no model training on tenant data.
no.root.home.privacy.processed[0]: Account email, to deliver one-time codes
no.root.home.privacy.processed[1]: Authentication events with technical metadata, kept for security and audit
no.root.home.privacy.processed[2]: Transient abuse-prevention counters that expire on their own
no.root.home.privacy.processed[3]: Credentials and cryptographic keys stored only in protected form
no.root.home.privacy.never[0]: Sell, rent, or share personal data — ever, for any purpose
no.root.home.privacy.never[1]: Load third-party trackers or ad pixels on auth surfaces
no.root.home.privacy.never[2]: Train models on tenant or end-user data
no.root.home.privacy.never[3]: Keep data after you close your account, beyond legal minimums
no.root.home.quickstart.title: Three requests to a working login.
no.root.home.quickstart.intro: No proprietary protocol, no vendor lock-in — everything below is stock OAuth 2.1 and OIDC against our live endpoints.
no.root.home.quickstart.steps[0].title: Discover our endpoints
no.root.home.quickstart.steps[0].body: Your app reads standard OIDC discovery — no SDK required, any language works.
no.root.home.quickstart.steps[1].title: Send users to /authorize with PKCE
no.root.home.quickstart.steps[1].body: Create a code challenge, redirect the browser, we handle the hosted login and email code.
no.root.home.quickstart.steps[2].title: Exchange the code for tokens
no.root.home.quickstart.steps[2].body: Verify the id_token against our public JWKS, keep the refresh token, call userinfo when you need claims.

no.root.home.pricing.intro: Early-access pricing. A monthly active user is a user who authenticated at least once that month; you are never billed for stored-but-idle accounts.
no.root.home.pricing.plans[0].features[3]: Audit ledger and auth event logs
no.root.home.pricing.plans[1].features[2]: MFA, passkeys, and enterprise SSO as they ship
no.root.home.pricing.note: Billing is not yet automated — early-access tenants are invoiced manually and can leave anytime.

no.root.home.ctaBand.body: Point discovery at auth.sdk.enterprises and ship your first flow this afternoon.
