no.root.legal.dpa.title: Data processing addendum
no.root.legal.dpa.description: This addendum sets out the terms on which SDK Enterprises processes personal data on behalf of tenants of the Auth service. It reflects the requirements applicable to processors under data protection law, including Article 28 of the General Data Protection Regulation.
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[0].heading: 1. Parties and roles
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[0].content[0]: This addendum is between you (the controller, "Customer") and SDK Enterprises (the processor). It applies to personal data that SDK Enterprises processes on your behalf when you use the Service to authenticate your end users. It forms part of the Agreement and prevails over it on matters of data protection.
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].heading: 2. Details of processing
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][0]: Subject matter: authentication and identity services for Customer applications.
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][1]: Duration: the term of the Agreement, plus retention duties described below.
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][2]: Nature and purpose: delivery of sign-in flows, verification of identity through one-time codes, issuance and management of sessions and tokens, abuse prevention, security logging, and associated support.
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][3]: Categories of data subjects: Customer's end users, and Customer personnel administering the tenant.
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][4]: Categories of personal data: identification data (notably email addresses), authentication and usage records, technical metadata such as IP address and user-agent, security and audit records, and transient abuse-prevention indicators.
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][5]: Special categories: none are requested or expected; Customer must not submit them.
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[2].heading: 3. Processor obligations
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[2].content[0]: SDK Enterprises processes personal data only on documented instructions from Customer — constituted by this addendum and Customer's configuration of the Service — unless required otherwise by Union or Member State law, in which case SDK Enterprises informs Customer of that legal requirement before processing unless legally prohibited. SDK Enterprises informs Customer without delay if it believes an instruction infringes applicable data protection law.
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[3].heading: 4. Confidentiality
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[3].content[0]: Persons authorised to process personal data do so only as necessary for the Service and are bound by confidentiality obligations that survive the end of their engagement.
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[4].heading: 5. Security measures
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[4].content[0]: Taking into account the state of the art and the costs of implementation, SDK Enterprises maintains appropriate technical and organisational measures, including: encryption of data in transit and appropriate encryption at rest; strict access control on a need-to-know basis; segregation of tenant environments; measures for availability and resilience, including backups and recovery procedures; abuse detection and rate limiting; tamper-evident logging of security-relevant events; and regular review of these measures as the Service evolves. A plain-language overview is published at /security.
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[5].heading: 6. Subprocessors
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[5].content[0]: Customer grants general written authorisation to engage subprocessors, whose identities, roles, and locations are published at /legal/subprocessors. SDK Enterprises imposes on each subprocessor, in writing, data protection obligations no less protective than those in this addendum and remains liable to Customer for subprocessor failures. At least fourteen (14) days before a new subprocessor processes personal data, SDK Enterprises updates the published list, giving Customer the opportunity to object on reasonable, data-protection-related grounds; if an objection cannot reasonably be resolved, Customer may terminate the affected part of the Service.
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].heading: 7. Assistance to Customer
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][0]: Requests from data subjects (access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection, portability): SDK Enterprises assists without undue delay, through available tenant tooling where possible.
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][1]: Data protection impact assessments and prior consultations: SDK Enterprises provides reasonably available information about the Service.
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][2]: Security incidents: SDK Enterprises notifies Customer without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting Customer's data, provides information reasonably required for Customer's own obligations, and cooperates in managing the incident.
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[7].heading: 8. International transfers
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[7].content[0]: Where personal data would be transferred outside the European Economic Area to a country not benefiting from an adequacy decision, SDK Enterprises ensures appropriate safeguards are in place — principally the standard contractual clauses adopted by the European Commission, entered into between the relevant exporter and importer — together with supplementary technical measures where needed. Current transfer locations are described on the subprocessors page.
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[8].heading: 9. Accountability and audits
no.root.legal.dpa.sections[8].content[0]: SDK Enterprises keeps records of processing activities within its scope and makes available documentation demonstrating compliance with this addendum. Customer may request such information once per year, and additionally following a personal data breach or a substantiated compliance concern. On-site audits, where granted, take place at Customer's cost, on reasonable notice, and subject to confidentiality and the protections owed to other customers.

no.root.legal.privacy.sections[0].heading: 1. Who we are

For end users who sign in to a product or service powered by Auth, our customer remains responsible for that processing as controller, and SDK Enterprises processes personal data on their documented instructions as a data processor, under our data processing addendum. If you are such an end user, your first point of contact is the product you were signing in to; we support them in answering your request without undue delay.

no.root.legal.privacy.sections[2].content[0: Account data. Email address and basic profile elements you or your provider choose to submit; authentication timestamps and usage counters relating to your account.

Authentication data. Records of sign-in attempts and outcomes, issuance and revocation of tokens and sessions, and related technical metadata (including IP address, browser user-agent, and precise timestamps) retained for security, abuse prevention, and evidence purposes.
Security records. Tamper-evident logs of security-relevant events associated with your account or environment.
Abuse-prevention data. Short-lived technical counters used to detect and throttle abusive traffic.
Communications data. The content of messages you send us (for example requests for support or the exercise of rights) and our replies.
Commercial data. Invoicing and payment references where a paid plan applies, handled through our invoicing process.

no.root.legal.privacy.sections[4].heading: 5. Retention

no.root.security.meta.title: Security
no.root.security.meta.description: How Auth secures authentication infrastructure: token architecture, key rotation, rate limiting, the hash-chained audit ledger, and how to report a vulnerability.
no.root.security.hero.title: Security is the mechanism list.
no.root.security.hero.lead: We do not ask you to trust marketing claims — every protection below names exactly how it works and where it runs. If we cannot describe the mechanism, we do not make the claim.
no.root.security.layers[0].title: Token architecture
no.root.security.layers[0].points[0]: Authorization codes require PKCE (S256) on every request and are single-use with short expiry.
no.root.security.layers[0].points[1]: Refresh tokens rotate on every use; presenting a consumed token revokes the entire token family.
no.root.security.layers[0].points[2]: Access and ID tokens are RS256 JWTs signed per environment; public keys are published at /.well-known/jwks.json.
no.root.security.layers[0].points[3]: Revocation is available at /oauth/revoke for refresh tokens.
no.root.security.layers[1].title: Sessions
no.root.security.layers[1].points[0]: Session cookies are http-only, SameSite=Lax, secure in production, and carry signed RS256 session JWTs.
no.root.security.layers[1].points[1]: Every session has both an idle timeout and an absolute expiry.
no.root.security.layers[1].points[2]: Sessions are revocable server-side; logout revokes immediately.
no.root.security.layers[2].title: Keys & secrets
no.root.security.layers[2].points[0]: Per-environment RS256 signing keys; private keys are envelope-encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) and never logged.
no.root.security.layers[2].points[1]: Rotation retires active keys while keeping them published so outstanding tokens verify until natural expiry.
no.root.security.layers[2].points[2]: Client secrets are stored only as encrypted material; verification is constant-time compared after decryption.
no.root.security.layers[3].title: Abuse controls
no.root.security.layers[3].points[0]: Fixed-window rate limits: code delivery per email and per IP, verification failures per email, token issuance per client and IP.
no.root.security.layers[3].points[1]: Excessive verification failures consume all outstanding one-time codes for that address.
no.root.security.layers[3].points[2]: User-facing error copy stays neutral; specifics are written to server logs only.
no.root.security.layers[4].title: Auditability
no.root.security.layers[4].points[0]: Security events are written to a per-environment hash-chained ledger: each entry commits to its predecessor by SHA-256.
no.root.security.layers[4].points[1]: The chain can be recomputed from genesis at any time; any retroactive edit breaks it.
no.root.security.layers[4].points[2]: Standard auth events (logins, token issuance, reuse detection, revocation, key creation) are recorded alongside the ledger.
no.root.security.layers[5].title: Data handling
no.root.security.layers[5].points[0]: Tenant data lives in a Neon Postgres database in the region selected for the deployment; access requires encrypted transport.
no.root.security.layers[5].points[1]: Secrets are envelope-encrypted before storage; the master key lives outside the database.
no.root.security.layers[5].points[2]: No third-party trackers or ad pixels run on auth surfaces; analytics on this marketing site are cookieless and aggregated.
no.root.security.complianceNote: Compliance status, honestly: Auth implements controls aligned with SOC 2 criteria from day one, but no certification audit has been completed yet. We will publish results here when that changes.
no.root.security.disclosure.title: Found a hole? Tell us.
no.root.security.disclosure.items[0]: Email hello@sdk.enterprises with [security] in the subject line.
no.root.security.disclosure.items[1]: Include reproduction steps; we acknowledge reports within 2 business days.
no.root.security.disclosure.items[2]: Please avoid automated scanning against production and do not access data beyond what proves the issue.
no.root.security.disclosure.items[3]: Good-faith research under this policy is safe from legal action; we credit reporters unless they prefer anonymity.

da.root.home.meta.title: Auth — multi-tenant authentication infrastructure

da.root.home.hero.visual.footnote: PKCE mandatory · tokens verified against public JWKS
da.root.home.standards.sentence: We implement the specs exactly: PKCE on every authorization code, rotating refresh tokens, revocable signed sessions, published signing keys.
da.root.home.features.title: Identity plumbing, handled.
da.root.home.features.intro: Everything below is live today unless marked otherwise — each card names the mechanism, because that is what you are actually buying.
da.root.home.features.items[0].title: Universal login
da.root.home.features.items[0].body: A hosted sign-in flow your users get redirected to — email one-time codes, no passwords to store, no login UI to maintain.
da.root.home.features.items[1].title: Session management
da.root.home.features.items[1].body: Sessions are signed RS256 JWTs in http-only cookies, with idle and absolute expiry, server-side revocation, and per-environment keys.
da.root.home.features.items[2].title: Token security
da.root.home.features.items[2].body: Authorization codes always travel with PKCE. Refresh tokens rotate on every use, and a replayed token revokes its whole family.
da.root.home.features.items[3].title: Audit ledger
da.root.home.features.items[3].body: Every security event lands in a hash-chained audit log per environment — tampering breaks the chain, and the chain recomputes from genesis.
da.root.home.features.items[4].title: Abuse controls
da.root.home.features.items[4].body: Fixed-window rate limits on code delivery, verification attempts, and token issuance. Lockouts consume outstanding codes; copy stays neutral.
da.root.home.features.items[5].title: Management API
da.root.home.features.items[5].body: One API surface for applications, users, sessions, and logs at /api/v2, driven by scoped machine tokens.
da.root.home.privacy.title: Your tenants' data stays yours.
da.root.home.privacy.intro: Auth is identity infrastructure — we process exactly what authentication requires and publish every detail. No ad trackers, no data sale, no model training on tenant data.
da.root.home.privacy.processed[0]: Account email, to deliver one-time codes
da.root.home.privacy.processed[1]: Authentication events with technical metadata, kept for security and audit
da.root.home.privacy.processed[2]: Transient abuse-prevention counters that expire on their own
da.root.home.privacy.processed[3]: Credentials and cryptographic keys stored only in protected form
da.root.home.privacy.never[0]: Sell, rent, or share personal data — ever, for any purpose
da.root.home.privacy.never[1]: Load third-party trackers or ad pixels on auth surfaces
da.root.home.privacy.never[2]: Train models on tenant or end-user data
da.root.home.privacy.never[3]: Keep data after you close your account, beyond legal minimums
da.root.home.quickstart.title: Three requests to a working login.
da.root.home.quickstart.intro: No proprietary protocol, no vendor lock-in — everything below is stock OAuth 2.1 and OIDC against our live endpoints.
da.root.home.quickstart.steps[0].title: Discover our endpoints
da.root.home.quickstart.steps[0].body: Your app reads standard OIDC discovery — no SDK required, any language works.
da.root.home.quickstart.steps[1].title: Send users to /authorize with PKCE
da.root.home.quickstart.steps[1].body: Create a code challenge, redirect the browser, we handle the hosted login and email code.
da.root.home.quickstart.steps[2].title: Exchange the code for tokens
da.root.home.quickstart.steps[2].body: Verify the id_token against our public JWKS, keep the refresh token, call userinfo when you need claims.

da.root.home.pricing.intro: Early-access pricing. A monthly active user is a user who authenticated at least once that month; you are never billed for stored-but-idle accounts.

da.root.home.pricing.plans[1].features[2]: MFA, passkeys, and enterprise SSO as they ship

da.root.home.ctaBand.body: Point discovery at auth.sdk.enterprises and ship your first flow this afternoon.

da.root.legal.dpa.title: Data processing addendum
da.root.legal.dpa.description: This addendum sets out the terms on which SDK Enterprises processes personal data on behalf of tenants of the Auth service. It reflects the requirements applicable to processors under data protection law, including Article 28 of the General Data Protection Regulation.
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[0].heading: 1. Parties and roles
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[0].content[0]: This addendum is between you (the controller, "Customer") and SDK Enterprises (the processor). It applies to personal data that SDK Enterprises processes on your behalf when you use the Service to authenticate your end users. It forms part of the Agreement and prevails over it on matters of data protection.
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].heading: 2. Details of processing
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][0]: Subject matter: authentication and identity services for Customer applications.
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][1]: Duration: the term of the Agreement, plus retention duties described below.
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][2]: Nature and purpose: delivery of sign-in flows, verification of identity through one-time codes, issuance and management of sessions and tokens, abuse prevention, security logging, and associated support.
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][3]: Categories of data subjects: Customer's end users, and Customer personnel administering the tenant.
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][4]: Categories of personal data: identification data (notably email addresses), authentication and usage records, technical metadata such as IP address and user-agent, security and audit records, and transient abuse-prevention indicators.
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][5]: Special categories: none are requested or expected; Customer must not submit them.
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[2].heading: 3. Processor obligations
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[2].content[0]: SDK Enterprises processes personal data only on documented instructions from Customer — constituted by this addendum and Customer's configuration of the Service — unless required otherwise by Union or Member State law, in which case SDK Enterprises informs Customer of that legal requirement before processing unless legally prohibited. SDK Enterprises informs Customer without delay if it believes an instruction infringes applicable data protection law.
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[3].heading: 4. Confidentiality
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[3].content[0]: Persons authorised to process personal data do so only as necessary for the Service and are bound by confidentiality obligations that survive the end of their engagement.
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[4].heading: 5. Security measures
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[4].content[0]: Taking into account the state of the art and the costs of implementation, SDK Enterprises maintains appropriate technical and organisational measures, including: encryption of data in transit and appropriate encryption at rest; strict access control on a need-to-know basis; segregation of tenant environments; measures for availability and resilience, including backups and recovery procedures; abuse detection and rate limiting; tamper-evident logging of security-relevant events; and regular review of these measures as the Service evolves. A plain-language overview is published at /security.
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[5].heading: 6. Subprocessors
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[5].content[0]: Customer grants general written authorisation to engage subprocessors, whose identities, roles, and locations are published at /legal/subprocessors. SDK Enterprises imposes on each subprocessor, in writing, data protection obligations no less protective than those in this addendum and remains liable to Customer for subprocessor failures. At least fourteen (14) days before a new subprocessor processes personal data, SDK Enterprises updates the published list, giving Customer the opportunity to object on reasonable, data-protection-related grounds; if an objection cannot reasonably be resolved, Customer may terminate the affected part of the Service.
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].heading: 7. Assistance to Customer
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][0]: Requests from data subjects (access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection, portability): SDK Enterprises assists without undue delay, through available tenant tooling where possible.
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][1]: Data protection impact assessments and prior consultations: SDK Enterprises provides reasonably available information about the Service.
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][2]: Security incidents: SDK Enterprises notifies Customer without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting Customer's data, provides information reasonably required for Customer's own obligations, and cooperates in managing the incident.
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[7].heading: 8. International transfers
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[7].content[0]: Where personal data would be transferred outside the European Economic Area to a country not benefiting from an adequacy decision, SDK Enterprises ensures appropriate safeguards are in place — principally the standard contractual clauses adopted by the European Commission, entered into between the relevant exporter and importer — together with supplementary technical measures where needed. Current transfer locations are described on the subprocessors page.
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[8].heading: 9. Accountability and audits
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[8].content[0]: SDK Enterprises keeps records of processing activities within its scope and makes available documentation demonstrating compliance with this addendum. Customer may request such information once per year, and additionally following a personal data breach or a substantiated compliance concern. On-site audits, where granted, take place at Customer's cost, on reasonable notice, and subject to confidentiality and the protections owed to other customers.
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[9].heading: 10. Return and deletion
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[9].content[0]: On termination of the Agreement, SDK Enterprises makes Customer's personal data available for export and then deletes it, including within subprocessor systems, within a commercially reasonable period — save where retention is required by law, in which case the data remains protected under this addendum until deletion becomes possible.
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[10].heading: 11. Liability, law, and disputes
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[10].content[0]: Liability under this addendum is allocated and limited as set out in the terms of service. This addendum is governed by French law, and disputes follow the resolution mechanism agreed there.
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[11].heading: 12. California privacy rights
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[11].content[0]: For personal data subject to the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended, SDK Enterprises acts as a service provider: it does not sell or share personal data, does not retain, use, or disclose it outside the direct business relationship except as permitted by law, and does not combine it with personal data received from other sources.
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[12].heading: 13. Precedence and amendments
da.root.legal.dpa.sections[12].content[0]: If individual provisions of this addendum conflict with the standard contractual clauses incorporated under section 8, the clauses prevail for the transfers they govern. We may amend this addendum prospectively to reflect changes in the Service or law, announcing material changes on this page before they take effect.

da.root.legal.privacy.title: Privacy policy
da.root.legal.privacy.description: This policy explains what personal data the Auth service processes, why it is processed, how long it is kept, who it is shared with, and the rights available to the people concerned. We have written it to be read and understood, not merely displayed.
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[0].heading: 1. Who we are
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[0].content[0: The Auth service (the "Service") is operated by SDK Enterprises (SADDEK Entreprises, RCS Paris 850 513 912, whose registered office is at 44 Rue Pasquier, 75008 Paris, France — "SDK Enterprises", "we", "us"). Our customers use the Service to authenticate their own users; this document describes how personal data flows through that arrangement and what each party is responsible for.
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[1].heading: 2. Our role depends on the situation
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[1].content[0: For visitors to this website and for individuals who open or administer an account with us, SDK Enterprises determines why and how personal data is processed and acts as a data controller.

For end users who sign in to a product or service powered by Auth, our customer remains responsible for that processing as controller, and SDK Enterprises processes personal data on their documented instructions as a data processor, under our data processing addendum. If you are such an end user, your first point of contact is the product you were signing in to; we support them in answering your request without undue delay.
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[2].heading: 3. Categories of personal data we process
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[2].content[0: Account data. Email address and basic profile elements you or your provider choose to submit; authentication timestamps and usage counters relating to your account.

Authentication data. Records of sign-in attempts and outcomes, issuance and revocation of tokens and sessions, and related technical metadata (including IP address, browser user-agent, and precise timestamps) retained for security, abuse prevention, and evidence purposes.
Security records. Tamper-evident logs of security-relevant events associated with your account or environment.
Abuse-prevention data. Short-lived technical counters used to detect and throttle abusive traffic.
Communications data. The content of messages you send us (for example requests for support or the exercise of rights) and our replies.
Commercial data. Invoicing and payment references where a paid plan applies, handled through our invoicing process.
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[2].content[1: We do not require or store passwords for sign-in to the Service. Sensitive categories of personal data (health, biometrics, political opinions, and similar) are not requested and must not be submitted to us.
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[3].heading: 4. Purposes and legal bases
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[3].content[0: Operating and providing the Service — performance of a contract, or steps prior to entering into one.
Securing accounts, detecting fraud and abuse, and keeping security records — our legitimate interest in operating trustworthy infrastructure, balanced against your rights and expectations.
Meeting accounting, tax, and other statutory duties — compliance with a legal obligation.
Sending service communications relating to your account or incidents affecting it — performance of the contract; we do not send marketing email absent separate consent.
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[3].content[1: Where processing relies on consent, you may withdraw it at any time without affecting the lawfulness of processing carried out before withdrawal. We do not carry out automated decision-making producing legal effects within the meaning of applicable law.
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[4].heading: 5. Retention
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[4].content[0: Personal data is kept only as long as necessary for the purposes set out above. Account data is kept while an account or tenant remains active; security and audit records are kept while needed to evidence the integrity of the Service and meet legal requirements; abuse-prevention data is transient by design; commercial records are kept for the statutorily required bookkeeping periods. Data that is no longer needed is deleted or irreversibly anonymised.
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[5].heading: 6. Recipients and subprocessors
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[5].content[0: We share personal data only with: processors acting under contract on our behalf (hosting, database, cache, and email-delivery providers — identified individually on our subprocessors page); professional advisers under duties of confidentiality; and public authorities where a binding legal request requires it, in which case we notify those concerned unless legally prohibited. We never sell, rent, or broker personal data, and we do not use customer or end-user data for advertising or for training machine-learning models.
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[6].heading: 7. International transfers
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[6].content[0: Some of our providers operate outside the European Economic Area. Where personal data is transferred out of the EEA, we rely on an adequate adequacy decision or on appropriate safeguards — in particular the European Commission's standard contractual clauses — together with supplementary measures where required. The current list of providers and their locations is published on our subprocessors page.
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[7].heading: 8. Security of processing
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[7].content[0: We apply appropriate technical and organisational measures against unauthorised access, loss, alteration, or disclosure — including encryption in transit and at rest, strict access controls on a need-to-know basis, segregation of tenant data, rate limiting and abuse detection, and tamper-evident audit logging. Measures are reviewed as the Service evolves; a plain-language overview is available on our security page.
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].heading: 9. Your rights
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[0: Subject to applicable law, including the General Data Protection Regulation if you are in the EEA, you may ask us to:
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[1: give you access to the personal data we hold about you;
rectify inaccurate data or complete incomplete data;
erase data that is no longer lawfully processed;
restrict or object to particular processing;
provide your data in a structured, commonly used, portable format;
tell you about the recipients of your data and the safeguards applied.
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[2: Write to hello@sdk.enterprises. We respond within one month of a substantiated request and may ask for minimal proof of identity where necessary. You may also lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority — in France, the Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CNIL).
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[9].heading: 10. Children
da.root.legal.privacy.sections[9].content[0: The Service is directed at businesses and professionals. We do not knowingly process the personal data of children below the age of digital consent in the relevant jurisdiction; if you believe this has happened, contact us and we will delete the data promptly.

da.root.security.meta.title: Security
da.root.security.meta.description: How Auth secures authentication infrastructure: token architecture, key rotation, rate limiting, the hash-chained audit ledger, and how to report a vulnerability.
da.root.security.hero.title: Security is the mechanism list.
da.root.security.hero.lead: We do not ask you to trust marketing claims — every protection below names exactly how it works and where it runs. If we cannot describe the mechanism, we do not make the claim.
da.root.security.layers[0].title: Token architecture
da.root.security.layers[0].points[0]: Authorization codes require PKCE (S256) on every request and are single-use with short expiry.
da.root.security.layers[0].points[1]: Refresh tokens rotate on every use; presenting a consumed token revokes the entire token family.
da.root.security.layers[0].points[2]: Access and ID tokens are RS256 JWTs signed per environment; public keys are published at /.well-known/jwks.json.
da.root.security.layers[0].points[3]: Revocation is available at /oauth/revoke for refresh tokens.
da.root.security.layers[1].title: Sessions
da.root.security.layers[1].points[0]: Session cookies are http-only, SameSite=Lax, secure in production, and carry signed RS256 session JWTs.
da.root.security.layers[1].points[1]: Every session has both an idle timeout and an absolute expiry.
da.root.security.layers[1].points[2]: Sessions are revocable server-side; logout revokes immediately.
da.root.security.layers[2].title: Keys & secrets
da.root.security.layers[2].points[0]: Per-environment RS256 signing keys; private keys are envelope-encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) and never logged.
da.root.security.layers[2].points[1]: Rotation retires active keys while keeping them published so outstanding tokens verify until natural expiry.
da.root.security.layers[2].points[2]: Client secrets are stored only as encrypted material; verification is constant-time compared after decryption.
da.root.security.layers[3].title: Abuse controls
da.root.security.layers[3].points[0]: Fixed-window rate limits: code delivery per email and per IP, verification failures per email, token issuance per client and IP.
da.root.security.layers[3].points[1]: Excessive verification failures consume all outstanding one-time codes for that address.
da.root.security.layers[3].points[2]: User-facing error copy stays neutral; specifics are written to server logs only.
da.root.security.layers[4].title: Auditability
da.root.security.layers[4].points[0]: Security events are written to a per-environment hash-chained ledger: each entry commits to its predecessor by SHA-256.
da.root.security.layers[4].points[1]: The chain can be recomputed from genesis at any time; any retroactive edit breaks it.
da.root.security.layers[4].points[2]: Standard auth events (logins, token issuance, reuse detection, revocation, key creation) are recorded alongside the ledger.
da.root.security.layers[5].title: Data handling
da.root.security.layers[5].points[0]: Tenant data lives in a Neon Postgres database in the region selected for the deployment; access requires encrypted transport.
da.root.security.layers[5].points[1]: Secrets are envelope-encrypted before storage; the master key lives outside the database.

fi.root.home.hero.title: One login flow for every tenant you host.
fi.root.home.hero.lead: Auth gives your product OIDC and OAuth 2.1 out of the box — hosted login pages, session management, and a management API — so your team ships features instead of identity plumbing.
fi.root.home.hero.visual.footnote: PKCE mandatory · tokens verified against public JWKS
fi.root.home.standards.sentence: We implement the specs exactly: PKCE on every authorization code, rotating refresh tokens, revocable signed sessions, published signing keys.
fi.root.home.features.title: Identity plumbing, handled.
fi.root.home.features.intro: Everything below is live today unless marked otherwise — each card names the mechanism, because that is what you are actually buying.
fi.root.home.features.items[0].title: Universal login
fi.root.home.features.items[0].body: A hosted sign-in flow your users get redirected to — email one-time codes, no passwords to store, no login UI to maintain.
fi.root.home.features.items[1].title: Session management
fi.root.home.features.items[1].body: Sessions are signed RS256 JWTs in http-only cookies, with idle and absolute expiry, server-side revocation, and per-environment keys.
fi.root.home.features.items[2].title: Token security
fi.root.home.features.items[2].body: Authorization codes always travel with PKCE. Refresh tokens rotate on every use, and a replayed token revokes its whole family.
fi.root.home.features.items[3].title: Audit ledger
fi.root.home.features.items[3].body: Every security event lands in a hash-chained audit log per environment — tampering breaks the chain, and the chain recomputes from genesis.
fi.root.home.features.items[4].title: Abuse controls
fi.root.home.features.items[4].body: Fixed-window rate limits on code delivery, verification attempts, and token issuance. Lockouts consume outstanding codes; copy stays neutral.
fi.root.home.features.items[5].title: Management API
fi.root.home.features.items[5].body: One API surface for applications, users, sessions, and logs at /api/v2, driven by scoped machine tokens.
fi.root.home.privacy.title: Your tenants' data stays yours.
fi.root.home.privacy.intro: Auth is identity infrastructure — we process exactly what authentication requires and publish every detail. No ad trackers, no data sale, no model training on tenant data.
fi.root.home.privacy.processed[0]: Account email, to deliver one-time codes
fi.root.home.privacy.processed[1]: Authentication events with technical metadata, kept for security and audit
fi.root.home.privacy.processed[2]: Transient abuse-prevention counters that expire on their own
fi.root.home.privacy.processed[3]: Credentials and cryptographic keys stored only in protected form
fi.root.home.privacy.never[0]: Sell, rent, or share personal data — ever, for any purpose
fi.root.home.privacy.never[1]: Load third-party trackers or ad pixels on auth surfaces
fi.root.home.privacy.never[2]: Train models on tenant or end-user data
fi.root.home.privacy.never[3]: Keep data after you close your account, beyond legal minimums
fi.root.home.quickstart.title: Three requests to a working login.
fi.root.home.quickstart.intro: No proprietary protocol, no vendor lock-in — everything below is stock OAuth 2.1 and OIDC against our live endpoints.
fi.root.home.quickstart.steps[0].title: Discover our endpoints
fi.root.home.quickstart.steps[0].body: Your app reads standard OIDC discovery — no SDK required, any language works.
fi.root.home.quickstart.steps[1].title: Send users to /authorize with PKCE
fi.root.home.quickstart.steps[1].body: Create a code challenge, redirect the browser, we handle the hosted login and email code.
fi.root.home.quickstart.steps[2].title: Exchange the code for tokens
fi.root.home.quickstart.steps[2].body: Verify the id_token against our public JWKS, keep the refresh token, call userinfo when you need claims.
fi.root.home.pricing.title: Priced by users, not by locks.
fi.root.home.pricing.intro: Early-access pricing. A monthly active user is a user who authenticated at least once that month; you are never billed for stored-but-idle accounts.
fi.root.home.pricing.plans[0].features[3]: Audit ledger and auth event logs
fi.root.home.pricing.plans[1].features[2]: MFA, passkeys, and enterprise SSO as they ship
fi.root.home.pricing.note: Billing is not yet automated — early-access tenants are invoiced manually and can leave anytime.
fi.root.home.ctaBand.title: Your login page is one redirect away.
fi.root.home.ctaBand.body: Point discovery at auth.sdk.enterprises and ship your first flow this afternoon.

fi.root.legal.dpa.title: Data processing addendum
fi.root.legal.dpa.description: This addendum sets out the terms on which SDK Enterprises processes personal data on behalf of tenants of the Auth service. It reflects the requirements applicable to processors under data protection law, including Article 28 of the General Data Protection Regulation.
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[0].heading: 1. Parties and roles
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[0].content[0]: This addendum is between you (the controller, "Customer") and SDK Enterprises (the processor). It applies to personal data that SDK Enterprises processes on your behalf when you use the Service to authenticate your end users. It forms part of the Agreement and prevails over it on matters of data protection.
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].heading: 2. Details of processing
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][0]: Subject matter: authentication and identity services for Customer applications.
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][1]: Duration: the term of the Agreement, plus retention duties described below.
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][2]: Nature and purpose: delivery of sign-in flows, verification of identity through one-time codes, issuance and management of sessions and tokens, abuse prevention, security logging, and associated support.
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][3]: Categories of data subjects: Customer's end users, and Customer personnel administering the tenant.
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][4]: Categories of personal data: identification data (notably email addresses), authentication and usage records, technical metadata such as IP address and user-agent, security and audit records, and transient abuse-prevention indicators.
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][5]: Special categories: none are requested or expected; Customer must not submit them.
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[2].heading: 3. Processor obligations
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[2].content[0]: SDK Enterprises processes personal data only on documented instructions from Customer — constituted by this addendum and Customer's configuration of the Service — unless required otherwise by Union or Member State law, in which case SDK Enterprises informs Customer of that legal requirement before processing unless legally prohibited. SDK Enterprises informs Customer without delay if it believes an instruction infringes applicable data protection law.
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[3].heading: 4. Confidentiality
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[3].content[0]: Persons authorised to process personal data do so only as necessary for the Service and are bound by confidentiality obligations that survive the end of their engagement.
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[4].heading: 5. Security measures
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[4].content[0]: Taking into account the state of the art and the costs of implementation, SDK Enterprises maintains appropriate technical and organisational measures, including: encryption of data in transit and appropriate encryption at rest; strict access control on a need-to-know basis; segregation of tenant environments; measures for availability and resilience, including backups and recovery procedures; abuse detection and rate limiting; tamper-evident logging of security-relevant events; and regular review of these measures as the Service evolves. A plain-language overview is published at /security.
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[5].heading: 6. Subprocessors
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[5].content[0]: Customer grants general written authorisation to engage subprocessors, whose identities, roles, and locations are published at /legal/subprocessors. SDK Enterprises imposes on each subprocessor, in writing, data protection obligations no less protective than those in this addendum and remains liable to Customer for subprocessor failures. At least fourteen (14) days before a new subprocessor processes personal data, SDK Enterprises updates the published list, giving Customer the opportunity to object on reasonable, data-protection-related grounds; if an objection cannot reasonably be resolved, Customer may terminate the affected part of the Service.
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].heading: 7. Assistance to Customer
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][0]: Requests from data subjects (access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection, portability): SDK Enterprises assists without undue delay, through available tenant tooling where possible.
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][1]: Data protection impact assessments and prior consultations: SDK Enterprises provides reasonably available information about the Service.
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][2]: Security incidents: SDK Enterprises notifies Customer without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting Customer's data, provides information reasonably required for Customer's own obligations, and cooperates in managing the incident.
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[7].heading: 8. International transfers
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[7].content[0]: Where personal data would be transferred outside the European Economic Area to a country not benefiting from an adequacy decision, SDK Enterprises ensures appropriate safeguards are in place — principally the standard contractual clauses adopted by the European Commission, entered into between the relevant exporter and importer — together with supplementary technical measures where needed. Current transfer locations are described on the subprocessors page.
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[8].heading: 9. Accountability and audits
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[8].content[0]: SDK Enterprises keeps records of processing activities within its scope and makes available documentation demonstrating compliance with this addendum. Customer may request such information once per year, and additionally following a personal data breach or a substantiated compliance concern. On-site audits, where granted, take place at Customer's cost, on reasonable notice, and subject to confidentiality and the protections owed to other customers.
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[9].heading: 10. Return and deletion
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[9].content[0]: On termination of the Agreement, SDK Enterprises makes Customer's personal data available for export and then deletes it, including within subprocessor systems, within a commercially reasonable period — save where retention is required by law, in which case the data remains protected under this addendum until deletion becomes possible.
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[10].heading: 11. Liability, law, and disputes
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[10].content[0]: Liability under this addendum is allocated and limited as set out in the terms of service. This addendum is governed by French law, and disputes follow the resolution mechanism agreed there.
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[11].heading: 12. California privacy rights
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[11].content[0]: For personal data subject to the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended, SDK Enterprises acts as a service provider: it does not sell or share personal data, does not retain, use, or disclose it outside the direct business relationship except as permitted by law, and does not combine it with personal data received from other sources.
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[12].heading: 13. Precedence and amendments
fi.root.legal.dpa.sections[12].content[0]: If individual provisions of this addendum conflict with the standard contractual clauses incorporated under section 8, the clauses prevail for the transfers they govern. We may amend this addendum prospectively to reflect changes in the Service or law, announcing material changes on this page before they take effect.

fi.root.legal.privacy.title: Privacy policy
fi.root.legal.privacy.description: This policy explains what personal data the Auth service processes, why it is processed, how long it is kept, who it is shared with, and the rights available to the people concerned. We have written it to be read and understood, not merely displayed.
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[0].heading: 1. Who we are
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[0].content[0: The Auth service (the "Service") is operated by SDK Enterprises (SADDEK Entreprises, RCS Paris 850 513 912, whose registered office is at 44 Rue Pasquier, 75008 Paris, France — "SDK Enterprises", "we", "us"). Our customers use the Service to authenticate their own users; this document describes how personal data flows through that arrangement and what each party is responsible for.
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[1].heading: 2. Our role depends on the situation
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[1].content[0: For visitors to this website and for individuals who open or administer an account with us, SDK Enterprises determines why and how personal data is processed and acts as a data controller.

For end users who sign in to a product or service powered by Auth, our customer remains responsible for that processing as controller, and SDK Enterprises processes personal data on their documented instructions as a data processor, under our data processing addendum. If you are such an end user, your first point of contact is the product you were signing in to; we support them in answering your request without undue delay.
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[2].heading: 3. Categories of personal data we process
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[2].content[0: Account data. Email address and basic profile elements you or your provider choose to submit; authentication timestamps and usage counters relating to your account.

Authentication data. Records of sign-in attempts and outcomes, issuance and revocation of tokens and sessions, and related technical metadata (including IP address, browser user-agent, and precise timestamps) retained for security, abuse prevention, and evidence purposes.
Security records. Tamper-evident logs of security-relevant events associated with your account or environment.
Abuse-prevention data. Short-lived technical counters used to detect and throttle abusive traffic.
Communications data. The content of messages you send us (for example requests for support or the exercise of rights) and our replies.
Commercial data. Invoicing and payment references where a paid plan applies, handled through our invoicing process.
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[2].content[1: We do not require or store passwords for sign-in to the Service. Sensitive categories of personal data (health, biometrics, political opinions, and similar) are not requested and must not be submitted to us.
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[3].heading: 4. Purposes and legal bases
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[3].content[0: Operating and providing the Service — performance of a contract, or steps prior to entering into one.
Securing accounts, detecting fraud and abuse, and keeping security records — our legitimate interest in operating trustworthy infrastructure, balanced against your rights and expectations.
Meeting accounting, tax, and other statutory duties — compliance with a legal obligation.
Sending service communications relating to your account or incidents affecting it — performance of the contract; we do not send marketing email absent separate consent.
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[3].content[1: Where processing relies on consent, you may withdraw it at any time without affecting the lawfulness of processing carried out before withdrawal. We do not carry out automated decision-making producing legal effects within the meaning of applicable law.
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[4].heading: 5. Retention
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[4].content[0: Personal data is kept only as long as necessary for the purposes set out above. Account data is kept while an account or tenant remains active; security and audit records are kept while needed to evidence the integrity of the Service and meet legal requirements; abuse-prevention data is transient by design; commercial records are kept for the statutorily required bookkeeping periods. Data that is no longer needed is deleted or irreversibly anonymised.
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[5].heading: 6. Recipients and subprocessors
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[5].content[0: We share personal data only with: processors acting under contract on our behalf (hosting, database, cache, and email-delivery providers — identified individually on our subprocessors page); professional advisers under duties of confidentiality; and public authorities where a binding legal request requires it, in which case we notify those concerned unless legally prohibited. We never sell, rent, or broker personal data, and we do not use customer or end-user data for advertising or for training machine-learning models.
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[6].heading: 7. International transfers
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[6].content[0: Some of our providers operate outside the European Economic Area. Where personal data is transferred out of the EEA, we rely on an adequate adequacy decision or on appropriate safeguards — in particular the European Commission's standard contractual clauses — together with supplementary measures where required. The current list of providers and their locations is published on our subprocessors page.
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[7].heading: 8. Security of processing
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[7].content[0: We apply appropriate technical and organisational measures against unauthorised access, loss, alteration, or disclosure — including encryption in transit and at rest, strict access controls on a need-to-know basis, segregation of tenant data, rate limiting and abuse detection, and tamper-evident audit logging. Measures are reviewed as the Service evolves; a plain-language overview is available on our security page.
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].heading: 9. Your rights
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[0: Subject to applicable law, including the General Data Protection Regulation if you are in the EEA, you may ask us to:
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[1: give you access to the personal data we hold about you;
rectify inaccurate data or complete incomplete data;
erase data that is no longer lawfully processed;
restrict or object to particular processing;
provide your data in a structured, commonly used, portable format;
tell you about the recipients of your data and the safeguards applied.
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[2: Write to hello@sdk.enterprises. We respond within one month of a substantiated request and may ask for minimal proof of identity where necessary. You may also lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority — in France, the Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CNIL).
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[9].heading: 10. Children
fi.root.legal.privacy.sections[9].content[0: The Service is directed at businesses and professionals. We do not knowingly process the personal data of children below the age of digital consent in the relevant jurisdiction; if you believe this has happened, contact us and we will delete the data promptly.

fi.root.security.meta.title: Security
fi.root.security.meta.description: How Auth secures authentication infrastructure: token architecture, key rotation, rate limiting, the hash-chained audit ledger, and how to report a vulnerability.
fi.root.security.hero.title: Security is the mechanism list.
fi.root.security.hero.lead: We do not ask you to trust marketing claims — every protection below names exactly how it works and where it runs. If we cannot describe the mechanism, we do not make the claim.
fi.root.security.layers[0].title: Token architecture
fi.root.security.layers[0].points[0]: Authorization codes require PKCE (S256) on every request and are single-use with short expiry.
fi.root.security.layers[0].points[1]: Refresh tokens rotate on every use; presenting a consumed token revokes the entire token family.
fi.root.security.layers[0].points[2]: Access and ID tokens are RS256 JWTs signed per environment; public keys are published at /.well-known/jwks.json.
fi.root.security.layers[0].points[3]: Revocation is available at /oauth/revoke for refresh tokens.
fi.root.security.layers[1].title: Sessions
fi.root.security.layers[1].points[0]: Session cookies are http-only, SameSite=Lax, secure in production, and carry signed RS256 session JWTs.
fi.root.security.layers[1].points[1]: Every session has both an idle timeout and an absolute expiry.
fi.root.security.layers[1].points[2]: Sessions are revocable server-side; logout revokes immediately.
fi.root.security.layers[2].title: Keys & secrets
fi.root.security.layers[2].points[0]: Per-environment RS256 signing keys; private keys are envelope-encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) and never logged.
fi.root.security.layers[2].points[1]: Rotation retires active keys while keeping them published so outstanding tokens verify until natural expiry.
fi.root.security.layers[2].points[2]: Client secrets are stored only as encrypted material; verification is constant-time compared after decryption.
fi.root.security.layers[3].title: Abuse controls
fi.root.security.layers[3].points[0]: Fixed-window rate limits: code delivery per email and per IP, verification failures per email, token issuance per client and IP.
fi.root.security.layers[3].points[1]: Excessive verification failures consume all outstanding one-time codes for that address.
fi.root.security.layers[3].points[2]: User-facing error copy stays neutral; specifics are written to server logs only.
fi.root.security.layers[4].title: Auditability
fi.root.security.layers[4].points[0]: Security events are written to a per-environment hash-chained ledger: each entry commits to its predecessor by SHA-256.
fi.root.security.layers[4].points[1]: The chain can be recomputed from genesis at any time; any retroactive edit breaks it.
fi.root.security.layers[4].points[2]: Standard auth events (logins, token issuance, reuse detection, revocation, key creation) are recorded alongside the ledger.
fi.root.security.layers[5].title: Data handling
fi.root.security.layers[5].points[0]: Tenant data lives in a Neon Postgres database in the region selected for the deployment; access requires encrypted transport.
fi.root.security.layers[5].points[1]: Secrets are envelope-encrypted before storage; the master key lives outside the database.
fi.root.security.layers[5].points[2]: No third-party trackers or ad pixels run on auth surfaces; analytics on this marketing site are cookieless and aggregated.
fi.root.security.complianceNote: Compliance status, honestly: Auth implements controls aligned with SOC 2 criteria from day one, but no certification audit has been completed yet. We will publish results here when that changes.
fi.root.security.disclosure.title: Found a hole? Tell us.
fi.root.security.disclosure.items[0]: Email hello@sdk.enterprises with [security] in the subject line.
fi.root.security.disclosure.items[1]: Include reproduction steps; we acknowledge reports within 2 business days.
fi.root.security.disclosure.items[2]: Please avoid automated scanning against production and do not access data beyond what proves the issue.
fi.root.security.disclosure.items[3]: Good-faith research under this policy is safe from legal action; we credit reporters unless they prefer anonymity.

pl.root.home.features.title: Identity plumbing, handled.
pl.root.home.features.intro: Everything below is live today unless marked otherwise — each card names the mechanism, because that is what you are actually buying.
pl.root.home.features.items[0].title: Universal login
pl.root.home.features.items[0].body: A hosted sign-in flow your users get redirected to — email one-time codes, no passwords to store, no login UI to maintain.
pl.root.home.features.items[1].title: Session management
pl.root.home.features.items[1].body: Sessions are signed RS256 JWTs in http-only cookies, with idle and absolute expiry, server-side revocation, and per-environment keys.
pl.root.home.features.items[2].title: Token security
pl.root.home.features.items[2].body: Authorization codes always travel with PKCE. Refresh tokens rotate on every use, and a replayed token revokes its whole family.
pl.root.home.features.items[3].title: Audit ledger
pl.root.home.features.items[3].body: Every security event lands in a hash-chained audit log per environment — tampering breaks the chain, and the chain recomputes from genesis.
pl.root.home.features.items[4].title: Abuse controls
pl.root.home.features.items[4].body: Fixed-window rate limits on code delivery, verification attempts, and token issuance. Lockouts consume outstanding codes; copy stays neutral.
pl.root.home.features.items[5].title: Management API
pl.root.home.features.items[5].body: One API surface for applications, users, sessions, and logs at /api/v2, driven by scoped machine tokens.
pl.root.home.privacy.title: Your tenants' data stays yours.
pl.root.home.privacy.intro: Auth is identity infrastructure — we process exactly what authentication requires and publish every detail. No ad trackers, no data sale, no model training on tenant data.

pl.root.home.privacy.processed[1]: Authentication events with technical metadata, kept for security and audit
pl.root.home.privacy.processed[2]: Transient abuse-prevention counters that expire on their own
pl.root.home.privacy.processed[3]: Credentials and cryptographic keys stored only in protected form

pl.root.home.privacy.never[1]: Load third-party trackers or ad pixels on auth surfaces
pl.root.home.privacy.never[2]: Train models on tenant or end-user data

pl.root.home.quickstart.steps[1].body: Create a code challenge, redirect the browser, we handle the hosted login and email code.
pl.root.home.quickstart.steps[2].title: Exchange the code for tokens
pl.root.home.quickstart.steps[2].body: Verify the id_token against our public JWKS, keep the refresh token, call userinfo when you need claims.

pl.root.legal.dpa.title: Data processing addendum
pl.root.legal.dpa.description: This addendum sets out the terms on which SDK Enterprises processes personal data on behalf of tenants of the Auth service. It reflects the requirements applicable to processors under data protection law, including Article 28 of the General Data Protection Regulation.
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[0].heading: 1. Parties and roles
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[0].content[0]: This addendum is between you (the controller, "Customer") and SDK Enterprises (the processor). It applies to personal data that SDK Enterprises processes on your behalf when you use the Service to authenticate your end users. It forms part of the Agreement and prevails over it on matters of data protection.
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].heading: 2. Details of processing
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][0]: Subject matter: authentication and identity services for Customer applications.
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][1]: Duration: the term of the Agreement, plus retention duties described below.
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][2]: Nature and purpose: delivery of sign-in flows, verification of identity through one-time codes, issuance and management of sessions and tokens, abuse prevention, security logging, and associated support.
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][3]: Categories of data subjects: Customer's end users, and Customer personnel administering the tenant.
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][4]: Categories of personal data: identification data (notably email addresses), authentication and usage records, technical metadata such as IP address and user-agent, security and audit records, and transient abuse-prevention indicators.
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][5]: Special categories: none are requested or expected; Customer must not submit them.
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[2].heading: 3. Processor obligations
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[2].content[0]: SDK Enterprises processes personal data only on documented instructions from Customer — constituted by this addendum and Customer's configuration of the Service — unless required otherwise by Union or Member State law, in which case SDK Enterprises informs Customer of that legal requirement before processing unless legally prohibited. SDK Enterprises informs Customer without delay if it believes an instruction infringes applicable data protection law.
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[3].heading: 4. Confidentiality
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[3].content[0]: Persons authorised to process personal data do so only as necessary for the Service and are bound by confidentiality obligations that survive the end of their engagement.
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[4].heading: 5. Security measures
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[4].content[0]: Taking into account the state of the art and the costs of implementation, SDK Enterprises maintains appropriate technical and organisational measures, including: encryption of data in transit and appropriate encryption at rest; strict access control on a need-to-know basis; segregation of tenant environments; measures for availability and resilience, including backups and recovery procedures; abuse detection and rate limiting; tamper-evident logging of security-relevant events; and regular review of these measures as the Service evolves. A plain-language overview is published at /security.
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[5].heading: 6. Subprocessors
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[5].content[0]: Customer grants general written authorisation to engage subprocessors, whose identities, roles, and locations are published at /legal/subprocessors. SDK Enterprises imposes on each subprocessor, in writing, data protection obligations no less protective than those in this addendum and remains liable to Customer for subprocessor failures. At least fourteen (14) days before a new subprocessor processes personal data, SDK Enterprises updates the published list, giving Customer the opportunity to object on reasonable, data-protection-related grounds; if an objection cannot reasonably be resolved, Customer may terminate the affected part of the Service.
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].heading: 7. Assistance to Customer
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][0]: Requests from data subjects (access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection, portability): SDK Enterprises assists without undue delay, through available tenant tooling where possible.
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][1]: Data protection impact assessments and prior consultations: SDK Enterprises provides reasonably available information about the Service.
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][2]: Security incidents: SDK Enterprises notifies Customer without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting Customer's data, provides information reasonably required for Customer's own obligations, and cooperates in managing the incident.
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[7].heading: 8. International transfers
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[7].content[0]: Where personal data would be transferred outside the European Economic Area to a country not benefiting from an adequacy decision, SDK Enterprises ensures appropriate safeguards are in place — principally the standard contractual clauses adopted by the European Commission, entered into between the relevant exporter and importer — together with supplementary technical measures where needed. Current transfer locations are described on the subprocessors page.
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[8].heading: 9. Accountability and audits
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[8].content[0]: SDK Enterprises keeps records of processing activities within its scope and makes available documentation demonstrating compliance with this addendum. Customer may request such information once per year, and additionally following a personal data breach or a substantiated compliance concern. On-site audits, where granted, take place at Customer's cost, on reasonable notice, and subject to confidentiality and the protections owed to other customers.
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[9].heading: 10. Return and deletion
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[9].content[0]: On termination of the Agreement, SDK Enterprises makes Customer's personal data available for export and then deletes it, including within subprocessor systems, within a commercially reasonable period — save where retention is required by law, in which case the data remains protected under this addendum until deletion becomes possible.
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[10].heading: 11. Liability, law, and disputes
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[10].content[0]: Liability under this addendum is allocated and limited as set out in the terms of service. This addendum is governed by French law, and disputes follow the resolution mechanism agreed there.
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[11].heading: 12. California privacy rights
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[11].content[0]: For personal data subject to the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended, SDK Enterprises acts as a service provider: it does not sell or share personal data, does not retain, use, or disclose it outside the direct business relationship except as permitted by law, and does not combine it with personal data received from other sources.
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[12].heading: 13. Precedence and amendments
pl.root.legal.dpa.sections[12].content[0]: If individual provisions of this addendum conflict with the standard contractual clauses incorporated under section 8, the clauses prevail for the transfers they govern. We may amend this addendum prospectively to reflect changes in the Service or law, announcing material changes on this page before they take effect.

pl.root.legal.privacy.title: Privacy policy
pl.root.legal.privacy.description: This policy explains what personal data the Auth service processes, why it is processed, how long it is kept, who it is shared with, and the rights available to the people concerned. We have written it to be read and understood, not merely displayed.
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[0].heading: 1. Who we are
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[0].content[0: The Auth service (the "Service") is operated by SDK Enterprises (SADDEK Entreprises, RCS Paris 850 513 912, whose registered office is at 44 Rue Pasquier, 75008 Paris, France — "SDK Enterprises", "we", "us"). Our customers use the Service to authenticate their own users; this document describes how personal data flows through that arrangement and what each party is responsible for.
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[1].heading: 2. Our role depends on the situation
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[1].content[0: For visitors to this website and for individuals who open or administer an account with us, SDK Enterprises determines why and how personal data is processed and acts as a data controller.

For end users who sign in to a product or service powered by Auth, our customer remains responsible for that processing as controller, and SDK Enterprises processes personal data on their documented instructions as a data processor, under our data processing addendum. If you are such an end user, your first point of contact is the product you were signing in to; we support them in answering your request without undue delay.
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[2].heading: 3. Categories of personal data we process
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[2].content[0: Account data. Email address and basic profile elements you or your provider choose to submit; authentication timestamps and usage counters relating to your account.

Authentication data. Records of sign-in attempts and outcomes, issuance and revocation of tokens and sessions, and related technical metadata (including IP address, browser user-agent, and precise timestamps) retained for security, abuse prevention, and evidence purposes.
Security records. Tamper-evident logs of security-relevant events associated with your account or environment.
Abuse-prevention data. Short-lived technical counters used to detect and throttle abusive traffic.
Communications data. The content of messages you send us (for example requests for support or the exercise of rights) and our replies.
Commercial data. Invoicing and payment references where a paid plan applies, handled through our invoicing process.
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[2].content[1: We do not require or store passwords for sign-in to the Service. Sensitive categories of personal data (health, biometrics, political opinions, and similar) are not requested and must not be submitted to us.
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[3].heading: 4. Purposes and legal bases
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[3].content[0: Operating and providing the Service — performance of a contract, or steps prior to entering into one.
Securing accounts, detecting fraud and abuse, and keeping security records — our legitimate interest in operating trustworthy infrastructure, balanced against your rights and expectations.
Meeting accounting, tax, and other statutory duties — compliance with a legal obligation.
Sending service communications relating to your account or incidents affecting it — performance of the contract; we do not send marketing email absent separate consent.
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[3].content[1: Where processing relies on consent, you may withdraw it at any time without affecting the lawfulness of processing carried out before withdrawal. We do not carry out automated decision-making producing legal effects within the meaning of applicable law.
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[4].heading: 5. Retention
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[4].content[0: Personal data is kept only as long as necessary for the purposes set out above. Account data is kept while an account or tenant remains active; security and audit records are kept while needed to evidence the integrity of the Service and meet legal requirements; abuse-prevention data is transient by design; commercial records are kept for the statutorily required bookkeeping periods. Data that is no longer needed is deleted or irreversibly anonymised.
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[5].heading: 6. Recipients and subprocessors
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[5].content[0: We share personal data only with: processors acting under contract on our behalf (hosting, database, cache, and email-delivery providers — identified individually on our subprocessors page); professional advisers under duties of confidentiality; and public authorities where a binding legal request requires it, in which case we notify those concerned unless legally prohibited. We never sell, rent, or broker personal data, and we do not use customer or end-user data for advertising or for training machine-learning models.
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[6].heading: 7. International transfers
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[6].content[0: Some of our providers operate outside the European Economic Area. Where personal data is transferred out of the EEA, we rely on an adequate adequacy decision or on appropriate safeguards — in particular the European Commission's standard contractual clauses — together with supplementary measures where required. The current list of providers and their locations is published on our subprocessors page.
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[7].heading: 8. Security of processing
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[7].content[0: We apply appropriate technical and organisational measures against unauthorised access, loss, alteration, or disclosure — including encryption in transit and at rest, strict access controls on a need-to-know basis, segregation of tenant data, rate limiting and abuse detection, and tamper-evident audit logging. Measures are reviewed as the Service evolves; a plain-language overview is available on our security page.
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].heading: 9. Your rights
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[0: Subject to applicable law, including the General Data Protection Regulation if you are in the EEA, you may ask us to:
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[1: give you access to the personal data we hold about you;
rectify inaccurate data or complete incomplete data;
erase data that is no longer lawfully processed;
restrict or object to particular processing;
provide your data in a structured, commonly used, portable format;
tell you about the recipients of your data and the safeguards applied.
pl.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[2: Write to hello@sdk.enterprises. We respond within one month of a substantiated request and may ask for minimal proof of identity where necessary. You may also lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority — in France, the Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CNIL).

pl.root.security.meta.title: Security
pl.root.security.meta.description: How Auth secures authentication infrastructure: token architecture, key rotation, rate limiting, the hash-chained audit ledger, and how to report a vulnerability.
pl.root.security.hero.title: Security is the mechanism list.
pl.root.security.hero.lead: We do not ask you to trust marketing claims — every protection below names exactly how it works and where it runs. If we cannot describe the mechanism, we do not make the claim.
pl.root.security.layers[0].title: Token architecture
pl.root.security.layers[0].points[0]: Authorization codes require PKCE (S256) on every request and are single-use with short expiry.
pl.root.security.layers[0].points[1]: Refresh tokens rotate on every use; presenting a consumed token revokes the entire token family.
pl.root.security.layers[0].points[2]: Access and ID tokens are RS256 JWTs signed per environment; public keys are published at /.well-known/jwks.json.
pl.root.security.layers[0].points[3]: Revocation is available at /oauth/revoke for refresh tokens.
pl.root.security.layers[1].title: Sessions
pl.root.security.layers[1].points[0]: Session cookies are http-only, SameSite=Lax, secure in production, and carry signed RS256 session JWTs.
pl.root.security.layers[1].points[1]: Every session has both an idle timeout and an absolute expiry.
pl.root.security.layers[1].points[2]: Sessions are revocable server-side; logout revokes immediately.
pl.root.security.layers[2].title: Keys & secrets
pl.root.security.layers[2].points[0]: Per-environment RS256 signing keys; private keys are envelope-encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) and never logged.
pl.root.security.layers[2].points[1]: Rotation retires active keys while keeping them published so outstanding tokens verify until natural expiry.
pl.root.security.layers[2].points[2]: Client secrets are stored only as encrypted material; verification is constant-time compared after decryption.
pl.root.security.layers[3].title: Abuse controls
pl.root.security.layers[3].points[0]: Fixed-window rate limits: code delivery per email and per IP, verification failures per email, token issuance per client and IP.
pl.root.security.layers[3].points[1]: Excessive verification failures consume all outstanding one-time codes for that address.
pl.root.security.layers[3].points[2]: User-facing error copy stays neutral; specifics are written to server logs only.
pl.root.security.layers[4].title: Auditability
pl.root.security.layers[4].points[0]: Security events are written to a per-environment hash-chained ledger: each entry commits to its predecessor by SHA-256.
pl.root.security.layers[4].points[1]: The chain can be recomputed from genesis at any time; any retroactive edit breaks it.
pl.root.security.layers[4].points[2]: Standard auth events (logins, token issuance, reuse detection, revocation, key creation) are recorded alongside the ledger.
pl.root.security.layers[5].title: Data handling
pl.root.security.layers[5].points[0]: Tenant data lives in a Neon Postgres database in the region selected for the deployment; access requires encrypted transport.
pl.root.security.layers[5].points[1]: Secrets are envelope-encrypted before storage; the master key lives outside the database.
pl.root.security.layers[5].points[2]: No third-party trackers or ad pixels run on auth surfaces; analytics on this marketing site are cookieless and aggregated.
pl.root.security.complianceNote: Compliance status, honestly: Auth implements controls aligned with SOC 2 criteria from day one, but no certification audit has been completed yet. We will publish results here when that changes.
pl.root.security.disclosure.title: Found a hole? Tell us.
pl.root.security.disclosure.items[0]: Email hello@sdk.enterprises with [security] in the subject line.
pl.root.security.disclosure.items[1]: Include reproduction steps; we acknowledge reports within 2 business days.
pl.root.security.disclosure.items[2]: Please avoid automated scanning against production and do not access data beyond what proves the issue.
pl.root.security.disclosure.items[3]: Good-faith research under this policy is safe from legal action; we credit reporters unless they prefer anonymity.
