bg.root.legal.dpa.title: Data processing addendum
bg.root.legal.dpa.description: This addendum sets out the terms on which SDK Enterprises processes personal data on behalf of tenants of the Auth service. It reflects the requirements applicable to processors under data protection law, including Article 28 of the General Data Protection Regulation.
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[0].heading: 1. Parties and roles
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[0].content[0]: This addendum is between you (the controller, "Customer") and SDK Enterprises (the processor). It applies to personal data that SDK Enterprises processes on your behalf when you use the Service to authenticate your end users. It forms part of the Agreement and prevails over it on matters of data protection.
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].heading: 2. Details of processing
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][0]: Subject matter: authentication and identity services for Customer applications.
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][1]: Duration: the term of the Agreement, plus retention duties described below.
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][2]: Nature and purpose: delivery of sign-in flows, verification of identity through one-time codes, issuance and management of sessions and tokens, abuse prevention, security logging, and associated support.
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][3]: Categories of data subjects: Customer's end users, and Customer personnel administering the tenant.
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][4]: Categories of personal data: identification data (notably email addresses), authentication and usage records, technical metadata such as IP address and user-agent, security and audit records, and transient abuse-prevention indicators.
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][5]: Special categories: none are requested or expected; Customer must not submit them.
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[2].heading: 3. Processor obligations
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[2].content[0]: SDK Enterprises processes personal data only on documented instructions from Customer — constituted by this addendum and Customer's configuration of the Service — unless required otherwise by Union or Member State law, in which case SDK Enterprises informs Customer of that legal requirement before processing unless legally prohibited. SDK Enterprises informs Customer without delay if it believes an instruction infringes applicable data protection law.
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[3].heading: 4. Confidentiality
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[3].content[0]: Persons authorised to process personal data do so only as necessary for the Service and are bound by confidentiality obligations that survive the end of their engagement.
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[4].heading: 5. Security measures
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[4].content[0]: Taking into account the state of the art and the costs of implementation, SDK Enterprises maintains appropriate technical and organisational measures, including: encryption of data in transit and appropriate encryption at rest; strict access control on a need-to-know basis; segregation of tenant environments; measures for availability and resilience, including backups and recovery procedures; abuse detection and rate limiting; tamper-evident logging of security-relevant events; and regular review of these measures as the Service evolves. A plain-language overview is published at /security.
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[5].heading: 6. Subprocessors
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[5].content[0]: Customer grants general written authorisation to engage subprocessors, whose identities, roles, and locations are published at /legal/subprocessors. SDK Enterprises imposes on each subprocessor, in writing, data protection obligations no less protective than those in this addendum and remains liable to Customer for subprocessor failures. At least fourteen (14) days before a new subprocessor processes personal data, SDK Enterprises updates the published list, giving Customer the opportunity to object on reasonable, data-protection-related grounds; if an objection cannot reasonably be resolved, Customer may terminate the affected part of the Service.
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].heading: 7. Assistance to Customer
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][0]: Requests from data subjects (access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection, portability): SDK Enterprises assists without undue delay, through available tenant tooling where possible.
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][1]: Data protection impact assessments and prior consultations: SDK Enterprises provides reasonably available information about the Service.
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][2]: Security incidents: SDK Enterprises notifies Customer without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting Customer's data, provides information reasonably required for Customer's own obligations, and cooperates in managing the incident.
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[7].heading: 8. International transfers
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[7].content[0]: Where personal data would be transferred outside the European Economic Area to a country not benefiting from an adequacy decision, SDK Enterprises ensures appropriate safeguards are in place — principally the standard contractual clauses adopted by the European Commission, entered into between the relevant exporter and importer — together with supplementary technical measures where needed. Current transfer locations are described on the subprocessors page.
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[8].heading: 9. Accountability and audits
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[8].content[0]: SDK Enterprises keeps records of processing activities within its scope and makes available documentation demonstrating compliance with this addendum. Customer may request such information once per year, and additionally following a personal data breach or a substantiated compliance concern. On-site audits, where granted, take place at Customer's cost, on reasonable notice, and subject to confidentiality and the protections owed to other customers.
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[9].heading: 10. Return and deletion
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[9].content[0]: On termination of the Agreement, SDK Enterprises makes Customer's personal data available for export and then deletes it, including within subprocessor systems, within a commercially reasonable period — save where retention is required by law, in which case the data remains protected under this addendum until deletion becomes possible.
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[10].heading: 11. Liability, law, and disputes
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[10].content[0]: Liability under this addendum is allocated and limited as set out in the terms of service. This addendum is governed by French law, and disputes follow the resolution mechanism agreed there.
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[11].heading: 12. California privacy rights
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[11].content[0]: For personal data subject to the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended, SDK Enterprises acts as a service provider: it does not sell or share personal data, does not retain, use, or disclose it outside the direct business relationship except as permitted by law, and does not combine it with personal data received from other sources.
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[12].heading: 13. Precedence and amendments
bg.root.legal.dpa.sections[12].content[0]: If individual provisions of this addendum conflict with the standard contractual clauses incorporated under section 8, the clauses prevail for the transfers they govern. We may amend this addendum prospectively to reflect changes in the Service or law, announcing material changes on this page before they take effect.

Security records. Tamper-evident logs of security-relevant events associated with your account or environment.

bg.root.legal.privacy.sections[7].heading: 8. Security of processing

bg.root.security.meta.title: Security
bg.root.security.meta.description: How Auth secures authentication infrastructure: token architecture, key rotation, rate limiting, the hash-chained audit ledger, and how to report a vulnerability.
bg.root.security.hero.title: Security is the mechanism list.
bg.root.security.hero.lead: We do not ask you to trust marketing claims — every protection below names exactly how it works and where it runs. If we cannot describe the mechanism, we do not make the claim.
bg.root.security.layers[0].title: Token architecture
bg.root.security.layers[0].points[0]: Authorization codes require PKCE (S256) on every request and are single-use with short expiry.
bg.root.security.layers[0].points[1]: Refresh tokens rotate on every use; presenting a consumed token revokes the entire token family.
bg.root.security.layers[0].points[2]: Access and ID tokens are RS256 JWTs signed per environment; public keys are published at /.well-known/jwks.json.
bg.root.security.layers[0].points[3]: Revocation is available at /oauth/revoke for refresh tokens.
bg.root.security.layers[1].title: Sessions
bg.root.security.layers[1].points[0]: Session cookies are http-only, SameSite=Lax, secure in production, and carry signed RS256 session JWTs.
bg.root.security.layers[1].points[1]: Every session has both an idle timeout and an absolute expiry.
bg.root.security.layers[1].points[2]: Sessions are revocable server-side; logout revokes immediately.
bg.root.security.layers[2].title: Keys & secrets
bg.root.security.layers[2].points[0]: Per-environment RS256 signing keys; private keys are envelope-encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) and never logged.
bg.root.security.layers[2].points[1]: Rotation retires active keys while keeping them published so outstanding tokens verify until natural expiry.
bg.root.security.layers[2].points[2]: Client secrets are stored only as encrypted material; verification is constant-time compared after decryption.
bg.root.security.layers[3].title: Abuse controls
bg.root.security.layers[3].points[0]: Fixed-window rate limits: code delivery per email and per IP, verification failures per email, token issuance per client and IP.
bg.root.security.layers[3].points[1]: Excessive verification failures consume all outstanding one-time codes for that address.
bg.root.security.layers[3].points[2]: User-facing error copy stays neutral; specifics are written to server logs only.
bg.root.security.layers[4].title: Auditability
bg.root.security.layers[4].points[0]: Security events are written to a per-environment hash-chained ledger: each entry commits to its predecessor by SHA-256.
bg.root.security.layers[4].points[1]: The chain can be recomputed from genesis at any time; any retroactive edit breaks it.
bg.root.security.layers[4].points[2]: Standard auth events (logins, token issuance, reuse detection, revocation, key creation) are recorded alongside the ledger.
bg.root.security.layers[5].title: Data handling
bg.root.security.layers[5].points[0]: Tenant data lives in a Neon Postgres database in the region selected for the deployment; access requires encrypted transport.
bg.root.security.layers[5].points[1]: Secrets are envelope-encrypted before storage; the master key lives outside the database.
bg.root.security.layers[5].points[2]: No third-party trackers or ad pixels run on auth surfaces; analytics on this marketing site are cookieless and aggregated.
bg.root.security.complianceNote: Compliance status, honestly: Auth implements controls aligned with SOC 2 criteria from day one, but no certification audit has been completed yet. We will publish results here when that changes.
bg.root.security.disclosure.title: Found a hole? Tell us.
bg.root.security.disclosure.items[0]: Email hello@sdk.enterprises with [security] in the subject line.
bg.root.security.disclosure.items[1]: Include reproduction steps; we acknowledge reports within 2 business days.
bg.root.security.disclosure.items[2]: Please avoid automated scanning against production and do not access data beyond what proves the issue.
bg.root.security.disclosure.items[3]: Good-faith research under this policy is safe from legal action; we credit reporters unless they prefer anonymity.

el.root.home.features.items[0].body: A hosted sign-in flow your users get redirected to — email one-time codes, no passwords to store, no login UI to maintain.

el.root.home.features.items[1].body: Sessions are signed RS256 JWTs in http-only cookies, with idle and absolute expiry, server-side revocation, and per-environment keys.
el.root.home.features.items[2].title: Token security
el.root.home.features.items[2].body: Authorization codes always travel with PKCE. Refresh tokens rotate on every use, and a replayed token revokes its whole family.
el.root.home.features.items[3].title: Audit ledger
el.root.home.features.items[3].body: Every security event lands in a hash-chained audit log per environment — tampering breaks the chain, and the chain recomputes from genesis.
el.root.home.features.items[4].title: Abuse controls
el.root.home.features.items[4].body: Fixed-window rate limits on code delivery, verification attempts, and token issuance. Lockouts consume outstanding codes; copy stays neutral.
el.root.home.features.items[5].title: Management API
el.root.home.features.items[5].body: One API surface for applications, users, sessions, and logs at /api/v2, driven by scoped machine tokens.

el.root.legal.dpa.title: Data processing addendum
el.root.legal.dpa.description: This addendum sets out the terms on which SDK Enterprises processes personal data on behalf of tenants of the Auth service. It reflects the requirements applicable to processors under data protection law, including Article 28 of the General Data Protection Regulation.
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[0].heading: 1. Parties and roles
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[0].content[0]: This addendum is between you (the controller, "Customer") and SDK Enterprises (the processor). It applies to personal data that SDK Enterprises processes on your behalf when you use the Service to authenticate your end users. It forms part of the Agreement and prevails over it on matters of data protection.
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].heading: 2. Details of processing
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][0]: Subject matter: authentication and identity services for Customer applications.
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][1]: Duration: the term of the Agreement, plus retention duties described below.
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][2]: Nature and purpose: delivery of sign-in flows, verification of identity through one-time codes, issuance and management of sessions and tokens, abuse prevention, security logging, and associated support.
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][3]: Categories of data subjects: Customer's end users, and Customer personnel administering the tenant.
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][4]: Categories of personal data: identification data (notably email addresses), authentication and usage records, technical metadata such as IP address and user-agent, security and audit records, and transient abuse-prevention indicators.
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[1].content[0][5]: Special categories: none are requested or expected; Customer must not submit them.
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[2].heading: 3. Processor obligations
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[2].content[0]: SDK Enterprises processes personal data only on documented instructions from Customer — constituted by this addendum and Customer's configuration of the Service — unless required otherwise by Union or Member State law, in which case SDK Enterprises informs Customer of that legal requirement before processing unless legally prohibited. SDK Enterprises informs Customer without delay if it believes an instruction infringes applicable data protection law.
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[3].heading: 4. Confidentiality
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[3].content[0]: Persons authorised to process personal data do so only as necessary for the Service and are bound by confidentiality obligations that survive the end of their engagement.
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[4].heading: 5. Security measures
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[4].content[0]: Taking into account the state of the art and the costs of implementation, SDK Enterprises maintains appropriate technical and organisational measures, including: encryption of data in transit and appropriate encryption at rest; strict access control on a need-to-know basis; segregation of tenant environments; measures for availability and resilience, including backups and recovery procedures; abuse detection and rate limiting; tamper-evident logging of security-relevant events; and regular review of these measures as the Service evolves. A plain-language overview is published at /security.
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[5].heading: 6. Subprocessors
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[5].content[0]: Customer grants general written authorisation to engage subprocessors, whose identities, roles, and locations are published at /legal/subprocessors. SDK Enterprises imposes on each subprocessor, in writing, data protection obligations no less protective than those in this addendum and remains liable to Customer for subprocessor failures. At least fourteen (14) days before a new subprocessor processes personal data, SDK Enterprises updates the published list, giving Customer the opportunity to object on reasonable, data-protection-related grounds; if an objection cannot reasonably be resolved, Customer may terminate the affected part of the Service.
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].heading: 7. Assistance to Customer
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][0]: Requests from data subjects (access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection, portability): SDK Enterprises assists without undue delay, through available tenant tooling where possible.
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][1]: Data protection impact assessments and prior consultations: SDK Enterprises provides reasonably available information about the Service.
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[6].content[0][2]: Security incidents: SDK Enterprises notifies Customer without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting Customer's data, provides information reasonably required for Customer's own obligations, and cooperates in managing the incident.
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[7].heading: 8. International transfers
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[7].content[0]: Where personal data would be transferred outside the European Economic Area to a country not benefiting from an adequacy decision, SDK Enterprises ensures appropriate safeguards are in place — principally the standard contractual clauses adopted by the European Commission, entered into between the relevant exporter and importer — together with supplementary technical measures where needed. Current transfer locations are described on the subprocessors page.
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[8].heading: 9. Accountability and audits
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[8].content[0]: SDK Enterprises keeps records of processing activities within its scope and makes available documentation demonstrating compliance with this addendum. Customer may request such information once per year, and additionally following a personal data breach or a substantiated compliance concern. On-site audits, where granted, take place at Customer's cost, on reasonable notice, and subject to confidentiality and the protections owed to other customers.
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[9].heading: 10. Return and deletion
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[9].content[0]: On termination of the Agreement, SDK Enterprises makes Customer's personal data available for export and then deletes it, including within subprocessor systems, within a commercially reasonable period — save where retention is required by law, in which case the data remains protected under this addendum until deletion becomes possible.
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[10].heading: 11. Liability, law, and disputes
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[10].content[0]: Liability under this addendum is allocated and limited as set out in the terms of service. This addendum is governed by French law, and disputes follow the resolution mechanism agreed there.
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[11].heading: 12. California privacy rights
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[11].content[0]: For personal data subject to the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended, SDK Enterprises acts as a service provider: it does not sell or share personal data, does not retain, use, or disclose it outside the direct business relationship except as permitted by law, and does not combine it with personal data received from other sources.
el.root.legal.dpa.sections[12].heading: 13. Precedence and amendments

We may amend this addendum prospectively to reflect changes in the Service or law, announcing material changes on this page before they take effect.

Security records. Tamper-evident logs of security-relevant events associated with your account or environment.

el.root.legal.privacy.sections[3].content[0: Operating and providing the Service — performance of a contract, or steps prior to entering into one.
Securing accounts, detecting fraud and abuse, and keeping security records — our legitimate interest in operating trustworthy infrastructure, balanced against your rights and expectations.
Meeting accounting, tax, and other statutory duties — compliance with a legal obligation.
Sending service communications relating to your account or incidents affecting it — performance of the contract; we do not send marketing email absent separate consent.
el.root.legal.privacy.sections[3].content[1: Where processing relies on consent, you may withdraw it at any time without affecting the lawfulness of processing carried out before withdrawal. We do not carry out automated decision-making producing legal effects within the meaning of applicable law.
el.root.legal.privacy.sections[4].heading: 5. Retention
el.root.legal.privacy.sections[4].content[0: Personal data is kept only as long as necessary for the purposes set out above. Account data is kept while an account or tenant remains active; security and audit records are kept while needed to evidence the integrity of the Service and meet legal requirements; abuse-prevention data is transient by design; commercial records are kept for the statutorily required bookkeeping periods. Data that is no longer needed is deleted or irreversibly anonymised.
el.root.legal.privacy.sections[5].heading: 6. Recipients and subprocessors
el.root.legal.privacy.sections[5].content[0: We share personal data only with: processors acting under contract on our behalf (hosting, database, cache, and email-delivery providers — identified individually on our subprocessors page); professional advisers under duties of confidentiality; and public authorities where a binding legal request requires it, in which case we notify those concerned unless legally prohibited. We never sell, rent, or broker personal data, and we do not use customer or end-user data for advertising or for training machine-learning models.
el.root.legal.privacy.sections[6].heading: 7. International transfers
el.root.legal.privacy.sections[6].content[0: Some of our providers operate outside the European Economic Area. Where personal data is transferred out of the EEA, we rely on an adequate adequacy decision or on appropriate safeguards — in particular the European Commission's standard contractual clauses — together with supplementary measures where required. The current list of providers and their locations is published on our subprocessors page.
el.root.legal.privacy.sections[7].heading: 8. Security of processing
el.root.legal.privacy.sections[7].content[0: We apply appropriate technical and organisational measures against unauthorised access, loss, alteration, or disclosure — including encryption in transit and at rest, strict access controls on a need-to-know basis, segregation of tenant data, rate limiting and abuse detection, and tamper-evident audit logging. Measures are reviewed as the Service evolves; a plain-language overview is available on our security page.
el.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].heading: 9. Your rights
el.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[0: Subject to applicable law, including the General Data Protection Regulation if you are in the EEA, you may ask us to:
el.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[1: give you access to the personal data we hold about you;
rectify inaccurate data or complete incomplete data;
erase data that is no longer lawfully processed;
restrict or object to particular processing;
provide your data in a structured, commonly used, portable format;
tell you about the recipients of your data and the safeguards applied.
el.root.legal.privacy.sections[8].content[2: Write to hello@sdk.enterprises. We respond within one month of a substantiated request and may ask for minimal proof of identity where necessary. You may also lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority — in France, the Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CNIL).
el.root.legal.privacy.sections[9].heading: 10. Children
el.root.legal.privacy.sections[9].content[0: The Service is directed at businesses and professionals. We do not knowingly process the personal data of children below the age of digital consent in the relevant jurisdiction; if you believe this has happened, contact us and we will delete the data promptly.

el.root.legal.privacy.sections[10].content[: We update this policy when our processing changes. Material changes are announced on this page, with a new effective date, before they take effect. Earlier versions are available on request.

el.root.security.meta.title: Security
el.root.security.meta.description: How Auth secures authentication infrastructure: token architecture, key rotation, rate limiting, the hash-chained audit ledger, and how to report a vulnerability.
el.root.security.hero.title: Security is the mechanism list.
el.root.security.hero.lead: We do not ask you to trust marketing claims — every protection below names exactly how it works and where it runs. If we cannot describe the mechanism, we do not make the claim.
el.root.security.layers[0].title: Token architecture
el.root.security.layers[0].points[0]: Authorization codes require PKCE (S256) on every request and are single-use with short expiry.
el.root.security.layers[0].points[1]: Refresh tokens rotate on every use; presenting a consumed token revokes the entire token family.
el.root.security.layers[0].points[2]: Access and ID tokens are RS256 JWTs signed per environment; public keys are published at /.well-known/jwks.json.
el.root.security.layers[0].points[3]: Revocation is available at /oauth/revoke for refresh tokens.
el.root.security.layers[1].title: Sessions
el.root.security.layers[1].points[0]: Session cookies are http-only, SameSite=Lax, secure in production, and carry signed RS256 session JWTs.
el.root.security.layers[1].points[1]: Every session has both an idle timeout and an absolute expiry.
el.root.security.layers[1].points[2]: Sessions are revocable server-side; logout revokes immediately.
el.root.security.layers[2].title: Keys & secrets
el.root.security.layers[2].points[0]: Per-environment RS256 signing keys; private keys are envelope-encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) and never logged.
el.root.security.layers[2].points[1]: Rotation retires active keys while keeping them published so outstanding tokens verify until natural expiry.
el.root.security.layers[2].points[2]: Client secrets are stored only as encrypted material; verification is constant-time compared after decryption.
el.root.security.layers[3].title: Abuse controls
el.root.security.layers[3].points[0]: Fixed-window rate limits: code delivery per email and per IP, verification failures per email, token issuance per client and IP.
el.root.security.layers[3].points[1]: Excessive verification failures consume all outstanding one-time codes for that address.
el.root.security.layers[3].points[2]: User-facing error copy stays neutral; specifics are written to server logs only.
el.root.security.layers[4].title: Auditability
el.root.security.layers[4].points[0]: Security events are written to a per-environment hash-chained ledger: each entry commits to its predecessor by SHA-256.
el.root.security.layers[4].points[1]: The chain can be recomputed from genesis at any time; any retroactive edit breaks it.
el.root.security.layers[4].points[2]: Standard auth events (logins, token issuance, reuse detection, revocation, key creation) are recorded alongside the ledger.
el.root.security.layers[5].title: Data handling
el.root.security.layers[5].points[0]: Tenant data lives in a Neon Postgres database in the region selected for the deployment; access requires encrypted transport.
el.root.security.layers[5].points[1]: Secrets are envelope-encrypted before storage; the master key lives outside the database.
el.root.security.layers[5].points[2]: No third-party trackers or ad pixels run on auth surfaces; analytics on this marketing site are cookieless and aggregated.
el.root.security.complianceNote: Compliance status, honestly: Auth implements controls aligned with SOC 2 criteria from day one, but no certification audit has been completed yet. We will publish results here when that changes.
el.root.security.disclosure.title: Found a hole? Tell us.
el.root.security.disclosure.items[0]: Email hello@sdk.enterprises with [security] in the subject line.
el.root.security.disclosure.items[1]: Include reproduction steps; we acknowledge reports within 2 business days.
el.root.security.disclosure.items[2]: Please avoid automated scanning against production and do not access data beyond what proves the issue.
el.root.security.disclosure.items[3]: Good-faith research under this policy is safe from legal action; we credit reporters unless they prefer anonymity.
